meta.title: Kingdom Inc Wiki
meta.extraction: Fresh ILSpy decompilation of the installed Assembly-CSharp.dll; current resources.assets English localization. No game assembly executed.
limitations: Static inspection does not validate Unity prefab settings, runtime mod patches or actual gameplay results.
Some definition fields are callbacks or dynamic expressions. They remain labeled in implementation details rather than being evaluated or assigned invented values.
Developer-only or hidden definitions are included and labeled where established by code. Presence in the assembly does not prove normal-game availability.
Icons use the existing local sprite export; mechanics and English text use the freshly inspected build.
Every source file is inventoried. Files without explanatory citations are listed explicitly in the audit.

Recent reports show that a strange corruption is seeping from deep within the cave, driving the beasts upwards towards the surface, driven mad with rage.

articles.title: Arlingen Farmstead
articles.summary: Stage 1 of Orcish Horde.

sections.title: Description
paragraphs: The former heartland of Yensburg's territory, with prime farmland crissccrossed by gentle streams. In better times the area provided a bounty of food to the population of Yensburg.

sections.title: Reward Description
paragraphs: Retake the farmstead to unlock the Farm tech!

sections.title: Reward Complete
paragraphs: Farm tech unlocked!

related.label: War Effort combat, medals, and defense

articles.title: Ruins of Arlingen
articles.summary: Stage 2 of Orcish Horde.

sections.title: Description
paragraphs: In ancient times these ruins were home to a large fortress, treasury, and prison complex. As the territory of Yensburg expanded the location was abandoned, and eventually overtaken by forces with nefarious intent.

sections.title: Reward Description
paragraphs: Retake the ruins to begin your descent into the Dungeon!

sections.title: Reward Complete
paragraphs: Dungeon tech unlocked!

related.label: War Effort combat, medals, and defense

articles.title: Terminus Gorge
articles.summary: Stage 3 of Orcish Horde.

sections.title: Description
paragraphs: For centuries, this dry gorge formed the eastern border of Yensburg's territory, a natural barrier separating it from the Hinterlands beyond. These days, the fortress at Terminus is deserted, save for a mad hermit that has managed to keep the orcs at bay.

sections.title: Reward Description
paragraphs: Retake the gorge to unlock the Summoning Circle tech!

sections.title: Reward Complete
paragraphs: Summoning Circle tech unlocked!

related.label: War Effort combat, medals, and defense

articles.title: Bastion
articles.summary: Stage 4 of Orcish Horde.

sections.title: Description
paragraphs: The fortress-city of Bastion was founded after the first expedition into the Hinterlands, centuries ago. The surrounding territory was subsequently conquered by orcs, but the city still defiantly maintains a human population.

sections.title: Reward Description
paragraphs: Retake Bastion to regain access to its Arena!

sections.title: Reward Complete
paragraphs: Arena tech unlocked!

related.label: War Effort combat, medals, and defense

articles.title: Orcish Horde
articles.summary: A brutish force that invaded Yensburg's territory from the east. Under their occupation, Yensburg is cut off from the fertile eastern lands, as well as the enormous fortress-city of Bastion.

sections.title: Campaign
paragraphs: A brutish force that invaded Yensburg's territory from the east. Under their occupation, Yensburg is cut off from the fertile eastern lands, as well as the enormous fortress-city of Bastion.

articles.title: Byrgenwald
articles.summary: Stage 1 of Southside Brigands.

sections.title: Description
paragraphs: The ancient forest of Byrgenwald has supplied Yensburg for many generations. Its massive trees provide the highest quality lumber, and the hunters that predate on the forest's many animals feed the hungry mouths in the city.

sections.title: Reward Description
paragraphs: Retake the forest to unlock the Forest tech!

sections.title: Reward Complete
paragraphs: Forest tech unlocked!

related.label: War Effort combat, medals, and defense

articles.title: Byrgenwald College
articles.summary: Stage 2 of Southside Brigands.

sections.title: Description
paragraphs: The austere scholars of the College have studied the applied sciences for decades. Within their hallowed library lie secrets that would enable the craftsmen of Yensburg to produce higher quality items.

sections.title: Reward Description
paragraphs: Retake the college to unlock Quality upgrades!

sections.title: Reward Complete
paragraphs: Quality upgrades unlocked!

related.label: War Effort combat, medals, and defense

articles.title: Feral Den
articles.summary: Stage 3 of Southside Brigands.

sections.title: Description
paragraphs: Many of the forest's most ferocious creatures live in the massive cave network known as the Feral Den. Rumor has it that a mysterious alpha monster leads the feral animals from deep within the Den.

sections.title: Reward Description
paragraphs: Unlock additional hunting and foraging options!

sections.title: Reward Complete
paragraphs: Hunting and foraging unlocked!

related.label: War Effort combat, medals, and defense

articles.title: Yensmouth
articles.summary: Stage 4 of Southside Brigands.

sections.title: Description
paragraphs: The famous port town of Yensmouth was once the home of the kingdom's Adventurer's Guild. However, with access cut off by the Southside Brigands, it has languished in obscurity for years.

sections.title: Reward Description
paragraphs: Retake Yensmouth to begin restoring the Adventurer's Guild!

sections.title: Reward Complete
paragraphs: Adventurer's Guild unlocked!

related.label: War Effort combat, medals, and defense

articles.title: Southside Brigands
articles.summary: A ragtag band of assorted criminals, brought together by a common cause: Plunder. They have occupied most of the ancient forest of Byrgenwald south of the city, cutting off contact with the forest dwellers and the port town of Yensmouth beyond.

sections.title: Campaign

articles.title: The Old Guildhouse
articles.summary: Stage 1 of Ironcrag Siege.

sections.title: Description
paragraphs: A vast mansion in the fields north of Yensburg that was once home to the Adventurer's Guild. For decades, it has been the home base of the treacherous Black Banner Legion mercenary band.

related.label: War Effort combat, medals, and defense

articles.title: Deadrock Pass
articles.summary: Stage 2 of Ironcrag Siege.

sections.title: Description
paragraphs: One of the few passable routes that lead further north, into the mountains. The natural chokepoint has been the end of several military campaigns in the past.

related.label: War Effort combat, medals, and defense

articles.title: Ironcrag Summit
articles.summary: Stage 3 of Ironcrag Siege.

sections.title: Description
paragraphs: As your army crests the mountain, they are shocked to discover its volcanic caldera. Lava spews forth from the earth and sinks back down in an endless churning lake of fire.

related.label: War Effort combat, medals, and defense

articles.title: Pinnacle Ruins
articles.summary: Stage 4 of Ironcrag Siege.

sections.title: Description
paragraphs: At the top of the mountain, a hidden path leads past the caldera and down into the earth. The enemy's stronghold has been exposed.

sections.title: Reward Description
paragraphs: Conquer the Pinnacle Ruins in order to descend into the Tomb of Sholrath.

sections.title: Reward Complete
paragraphs: The path to the Tomb has been breached!

related.label: War Effort combat, medals, and defense

articles.title: Combat stats and power
articles.summary: How rolled stats, equipment, quality, class multipliers, and damage traits combine.

sections.title: Eight stats
paragraphs: Health is damage capacity, Armor reduces ordinary incoming damage, Strength/Dexterity/Magic/Wisdom supply class power and skill checks, Energy limits adventurer activity, and Combat Power is a separate bonus added to a human’s main combat stat.
An unclassed human uses the highest of Strength, Dexterity, and Magic; ties favor Strength, then Dexterity. A class with an assigned PowerStat uses that instead, including Wisdom for cleric classes.

Human power = round((main stat + Combat Power bonus) × class multiplier × exhaustion multiplier). At zero energy, a human with an energy pool uses an exhaustion multiplier of 0.75. A nonhuman combatant instead uses round(Combat Power stat × its type multiplier). Base damage = round(power × active damage-trait multiplier). Activities then apply their own damage scaling and random rolls.

sections.title: Rolls and quality
paragraphs: Initial combatant stats range from floor(0.75 × declared base) through ceil(1.333 × base), using rounded interpolation. Energy has a fixed declared base. The basic Adventurer has base 100 Health, 100 Energy, and 40 Strength, Dexterity, Magic, and Wisdom.

For human stats, add stored base and all equipment contributions, apply active stat traits, then multiply by human quality and round. Energy is rounded without human-quality multiplication. A human with zero stored base Energy remains without an energy pool even if equipment supplies Energy. Health also receives the Human Health prestige multiplier before quality.

Equipment has independent quality and rolls. Its final stats are added before the wearer-quality multiplier, so both can compound. Health and energy are stored as fractions; changing the maximum retains the fraction.

sections.title: Class power multipliers
paragraphs: These declared values precede damage traits.

rows: Guardian, Battlemaster / Thief, Ranger / Elementalist, Warlock

sections.title: Critical damage
paragraphs: Critical Hit rolls a 5% × active trait quality chance whenever its damage multiplier is evaluated. A success doubles the current damage multiplier. Multiple sources of this same trait keep only the highest-quality active source. The weapon critical enchantment supplies this trait.

articles.title: Armor and damage reduction
articles.summary: The exact armor curve, unarmored penalty, and damage-processing order.

sections.title: Armor curve
paragraphs: For Armor A ≤ 200, ordinary incoming damage is multiplied by 0.5^(A/200). Above 200, first replace A with 200 + (A − 200)^0.8, then apply that exponential. This gives diminishing returns beyond 200.

Exactly zero Armor adds an extra ×2 penalty. Armor-ignoring attacks skip both the curve and zero-armor penalty. Active damage-taken traits apply afterward; the result is rounded and subtracted from health. An incoming value of exactly zero returns immediately.

sections.title: Roles and category
paragraphs: Tank multiplies damage taken by 0.75. Guardian with a Shield divides it by 1 + 0.1 × trait quality. These apply after armor and also protect against armor-ignoring attacks.
Armor category is distinct from the numerical Armor stat. Light, Medium, and Heavy tags affect advancement and certain traits. The numerical stat controls the damage curve.

articles.title: Skill tests and elemental resistances
articles.summary: Check probability, group checks, and the scope of resistance.

sections.title: Checks
paragraphs: Base success chance = clamp(stat ÷ difficulty, 5%, 95%). Skill-test traits modify this afterward. The four skill-critical traits each add 0.4 × trait quality for their matching stat; the final chance is not re-clamped to 95%. The random helper guarantees success when a final probability reaches 1.

Dungeon individual difficulty is integer StageDifficulty ÷ 4; group difficulty is integer StageDifficulty ÷ 3. Most group challenges let members try in order until one succeeds. Clear Rubble instead uses individual difficulty even though any member can save the group.

sections.title: Resistance
paragraphs: Fire, Shadow, and Poison resistance each use reduction = 0.3 + 0.2 × active trait quality, giving 50% at quality 1. The matching hazard multiplies its damage by 1 − reduction. Identical resistance traits keep the highest-quality source, not their sum.

Resistance is requested explicitly by particular hazards rather than universally applied to every elemental-sounding attack. Tank Shadow Damage computes Shadow resistance for its display but does not multiply the actual damage by it in this implementation. The formula contains no explicit upper clamp.

related.label: Energy, death, and dungeon limit breaks

articles.title: Traits and party buffs
articles.summary: Where trait strength comes from and how repeated effects combine.

sections.title: Sources
paragraphs: Traits come from archetypes, classes, equipment, enhancements, and temporary party buffs. Archetype traits use character quality. Declared class traits are instantiated at quality 1, so training does not directly strengthen their percentage formulas; it still improves underlying stats.

Equipment traits use item quality; enhancement traits use enhancement quality. A group buff retains its source trait quality. Repeated copies of the same trait keep only the highest quality. Different traits modify their shared value in stored order.

sections.title: Party application and clearing
paragraphs: At dungeon start every member applies group effects to every member, including themselves. Quest and War Effort intake apply the current members’ effects to the incoming member. Thus a newly added aura source should not be assumed to buff all earlier quest or war members retroactively.

ActivityCompleted increments Level and refreshes traits while clearing temporary buffs. Full Healers are healed completely. The Level counter itself is not an automatic per-level stat formula here; quality training is separate.
Equipment changes refresh traits while retaining stored buffs. Removing a buff removes one stored entry; consumed-aura behavior also depends on refresh and cleanup calls.

related.label: Energy, death, and dungeon limit breaks

articles.title: Tanks, healers, and party formation
articles.summary: Tank qualification, targeting odds, and automatic healing.

sections.title: Tank role
paragraphs: Fighter-archetype humans qualify as Tanks with an offhand Shield and Heavy armor qualification. This includes Fighter-derived classes. Tank reduces damage taken by 25%. The first qualifying member is the dungeon’s designated tank.

Ordinary dungeon hits select that tank with 85% probability on bosses or 65% on other stages, otherwise they select a random member. The random selection can also choose the tank. Scripted tank hazards use their own direct selection.
The displayed distance rank puts Tanks first, then melee or unarmed humans, then ranged humans. Ordinary targeting uses the probabilities above rather than a general front-row shield rule.

sections.title: Standard healing
paragraphs: Base healing starts at Wisdom. If the caster has Healer and combat power exceeds Wisdom, add half the difference using integer division. Apply healing-done multipliers and round. The normal spell heals base healing ÷ 10 using integer division, with the recipient’s healing-taken traits applied afterward.

It chooses the eligible member with the lowest health fraction; full-health and Exhausted members are excluded. A dungeon uses its first Healer, and can stay on a cleared stage while that caster continues finding wounded targets. The final stage ends before this healing phase.

Quest progress ticks have a 25% chance to request that spell. Wars allow a rounded one-Healer-per-five-soldiers limit, clamped to 1–10, randomly excluding excess healers each tick. Inquisitor has Minor Healer rather than the full role.

related.label: Energy, death, and dungeon limit breaks

articles.title: Adventurer classes and advancement routes
articles.summary: The complete class tree and its equipment conditions.

sections.title: First specialization
paragraphs: With Training Grounds specialization research, an Adventurer is checked halfway through training unless the energy payment just exhausted it. The first matching declared advancement wins.

rows: Main weapon’s declared main stat Strength; Heavy armor qualification
Main weapon’s declared main stat Dexterity; Medium armor qualification
Main weapon’s declared main stat Magic; Light armor qualification
Main weapon’s declared main stat Wisdom; no armor condition

sections.title: Quest branches
paragraphs: Fighter branches to Guardian or Battlemaster; Rogue to Thief or Ranger; Mage to Elementalist or Warlock; Cleric to Ritualist or Priest. The eight advancement quests change only members whose type exactly matches the required base class. Repeat quest rewards retain the advancement effect.

sections.title: Final specializations
paragraphs: Arena advancement checks choose the first eligible declared route after a bout.

rows: Arena; equipped main-hand item has positive actual Strength appraiser stat

sections.title: Armor qualification
paragraphs: Only Head, Chest, and Off Hand participate. At least one of Head or Chest must be present, and at least one must match the requested category. None of the checked pieces may have a category above the requested one. A lighter partner piece is allowed; a completely unarmored character does not qualify.
A weapon’s main stat is the first largest declared BaseStats entry in stat enum order. Inquisitor’s condition is different: it checks the actual equipped weapon’s Strength value.

related.label: Equipment slots, hands, and armor affinity

articles.title: Class trait effects
articles.summary: Implemented role bonuses for every specialization, separate from power multipliers.

sections.title: Parent traits
paragraphs: Here q is trait quality, normally fixed at 1 for declared class traits. Final classes retain their parent trait.

sections.title: Final effects
paragraphs: These add to retained parent traits.

rows: 50% chance per dungeon healing hook: heal lowest-health eligible ally other than self for base healing ÷ 20
Armor gains actual offhand Shield Armor × q
Without Heavy armor qualification: damage multiplier × (1 + 0.2q)
Dungeon group buff: boss damage multiplier × (1 + 0.03q)
Dungeon Tank group buff: boss damage taken × (1 − 0.1q)
Dungeon damage multiplier gains +0.15q; companion is not a separate combatant
Combat Power bonus gains 0.5 × current Strength × q; Minor Healer role
33.3% chance per dungeon healing hook: heal every member for base healing ÷ 40
Dungeon Tank group buff: healing received on boss stages × (1 + 0.1q)

sections.title: Healer inheritance
paragraphs: Cleric, Ritualist, Priest, Shaman, Evangelist, and Lightbringer declare full Healer. Inquisitor instead has Minor Healer: 50% chance on dungeon-healing and war hooks to heal an eligible ally other than self for base healing ÷ 25. Fighter-archetype descendants can gain Tank through equipment regardless of branch.

articles.title: Equipment slots, hands, and armor affinity
articles.summary: Slot unlocks, weapon conflicts, equipment rolls, and enhancements.

sections.title: Unlocks
paragraphs: Head, Chest, Main Hand, and Off Hand are available by default. Food requires Campfire, Adventure Supplies, or Kitchen; Potion requires Adventure Supplies or Alchemist; Amulet/Ring require Jeweler; Trinket requires Inventor; Scroll requires Scribe.

The equipment gate supports a per-type EquipmentAllowed predicate, but the extracted source contains no assignments to it. Class affinity is primarily an advancement or trait condition rather than a general ban on other equipment.

sections.title: Weapon handling
paragraphs: Greatsword, Bow, Rifle, Staff, and Battleaxe are two-handed. Sword and Dagger are ambidextrous. Shield, Tome, and Focus are Off Hand. Bow, Rifle, Staff, and Wand are ranged for distance rank.
HasWeapon requires a main-hand WeaponItemType. HasDualWield counts more than one such weapon entry. HasShield searches for any Shield weapon. Adding equipment removes conflicts and refreshes traits.

sections.title: Equipment and enhancements
paragraphs: Equipment stat ranges are floor(base × 0.9 × item quality) to ceil(base × 1.1 × item quality). Integer rolls exclude the upper endpoint when bounds differ. Updating equipment quality rerolls these base stats. Enhancement stats are added afterward.

Without multi-enhancement research only one enhancement is allowed. With it, one enhancement per EnhancementType is allowed; duplicate types remain disallowed. Equipment and enhancement traits also contribute their own effects.

Each flat enhancement stat is round(declared enhancement stat × enhancement quality) before being added to the equipment. This differs from the equipment’s own rolled base stats. Quality-adding enhancements affect the item through their crafting workflow; trait quality remains the enhancement source’s quality.

articles.title: Training Grounds and quality growth
articles.summary: Sessions, dummies, food, repeat energy costs, and specialization timing.

sections.title: Session
paragraphs: A session has 10 training ticks, normally every 2 ÷ Speed seconds. A manual action independently has a 50% chance to tick each occupied slot. The Capacity property starts at 3 and rises to 5 with research; intake scans the full five-slot array, so the property alone does not establish an enforced cap.
Each tick requests quality gain of QualityPerTick × building quality, affected by training traits, then awards a random half-to-full share. QualityPerTick is 0.02 without a dummy, 0.04 with one.

Ordinary humans get full gain in their first session, half in their second, and zero from the third onward. Adventurers retain full gain. A nonhuman dummy takes trainee base damage ÷ 10 on ticks with positive gain multiplier; dead dummies are removed.

sections.title: Energy and food
paragraphs: Each tick costs 2 × (1 + TrainingCount) Energy before traits. With food research and Food equipped this is halved; automatic training also performs a second tick for food-bearing trainees each cycle. Food is consumed at completion while that technology is active.

At halfway, specialization research checks advancement if the energy payment did not exhaust the trainee. Exhausted trainees are removed. Finished trainees wait for output space, receive ActivityCompleted, and increase TrainingCount (ordinary humans stop incrementing at 3).

sections.title: War cleanup
paragraphs: War Effort separately cleans non-adventurer humans with TrainingCount above 4: the count becomes 4 and quality is capped at 1.5. This differs from ordinary training diminishing returns.

articles.title: Arena combat and training
articles.summary: Damage, bout-ending conditions, training ticks, and survivor outputs.

sections.title: Attacks
paragraphs: Arena accepts two combatants and its normal update is blocked until Eastern war stage 4 is held. Each fighter applies group buffs only to itself. Attacks occur every 2 ÷ Speed seconds.

Each base damage is integer-divided by 10, then rolled from that value ÷ 1.2 to ×1.2 before armor and damage-taken traits. Both attack values are calculated before damage is applied. Trait hooks run after both hits.

sections.title: Ending a fight
paragraphs: Normal bouts end when a human is below 10% health or a nonhuman dies. Humans that reached zero in normal mode receive a small 2–4 health heal at the next stopping check. Blood Sport waits for a death; if both die, one randomly receives the small heal.

The 10-tick counter limits training and energy deductions, not total bout duration. After it reaches zero, attacks continue until a health ending condition. Opponents whose damage rounds to zero or whose healing outpaces damage may stall.

Eligible humans gain a random half-to-full share of the quality request for each of those first 10 attacks. They pay 3 × (1 + ArenaCount) Energy. Adventurers stay eligible across bouts; ordinary humans train only on their first. Other combatants pay the base energy cost when they have an energy pool.

rows: 0.06; actual quality gain still requires an eligible human

sections.title: Outputs
paragraphs: Only living, non-Exhausted humans return: adventurers repeatedly, ordinary humans only from their first arena visit. Resolution waits for eligible outputs to have room. Returning humans receive ActivityCompleted and ArenaCount increases.

The winner uses higher health fraction; ties select slot 2. Arena and ArenaWin advancement routes are checked in declaration order after output handling. The bout then pays its audience reward and clears both slots.

articles.title: Arena audience income
articles.summary: How initial health, weapons, fighter types, and upgrades determine bout payment.

sections.title: Reward multiplier
paragraphs: At fight start, multiply both fighters’ current health fractions. Halve that result for each human without a main-hand weapon. This initial value is retained until resolution, so starting wounded reduces the entire bout’s reward.

At resolution, multiply by 1 + 0.1 × Arena Cashier upgrade count. Each Adventurer then contributes ×1.2; each other human contributes ×1.1; nonhumans add no type multiplier. With Blood Sport, a multiplier above 1 receives another ×1.25.

sections.title: Payment currency
paragraphs: Currency is selected with successive independent 25% checks, gated by strict reward thresholds. First try Ducats if the multiplier exceeds 1.5; if that fails or is unavailable, try Rings above 1.25, then Crowns above 1.09. Otherwise pay Gold.

Payment count is round(10,000 × final reward multiplier ÷ selected currency’s gold value). This changes the denomination, while the formula targets the same gold-equivalent amount. A resolved bout sets a four-second cooldown.

articles.title: Quest Board progress and repeat costs
articles.summary: Five-adventurer work groups, progress-based hazards, energy, training, and blocked outputs.

sections.title: Progress
paragraphs: A Quest Board holds up to five adventurers and updates once per second. Each living, non-Exhausted participant contributes base damage ÷ its individually adjusted quest difficulty. For quests with DurationMultiplier exactly 1, the contribution is capped at 2 per participant per update.

A contribution below 1 is penalized: the adventurer takes a random damage roll around 0.5 ÷ its original contribution (range ÷1.5 to ×1.5), then contributes only half the original amount. This makes badly underpowered adventurers both slower and vulnerable.

Progress is shared. Challenges and trait hooks execute once for each whole progress boundary crossed, not once per real second. Faster groups therefore run more hazard and energy ticks per second while finishing sooner. Progress may overshoot the target.

sections.title: Energy and completion
paragraphs: Each whole progress tick costs EnergyPerTick × (1 + that adventurer’s QuestCount), before positive-energy-loss trait modifiers. The default EnergyPerTick is 0.2. Hazards may add to it. A 25% chance on each progress tick asks the first Healer to cast.

Completion waits until every output buffer is empty. It subtracts the quest’s current TickDuration from shared progress, grants first or repeat rewards, increments global completion count, then returns all current members through the adventurer output.

Each returned member receives the quest’s completion callback, ActivityCompleted, +1 QuestCount, and a random half-to-full quality gain from TrainingAdded × training upgrade multiplier. Default TrainingAdded is 0.12; each Quest Training upgrade adds +0.5 to the multiplier. Coin upgrades add +0.1 each to the currency multiplier.

sections.title: Repeated duration
paragraphs: TickDuration = round(BaseDuration × DurationMultiplier^global completion count). Only quests with a multiplier other than 1 grow this way, and those quests also bypass the normal contribution cap of 2. This count belongs to the quest metadata, so different boards share its first-clear and repeat history.

Dead or Exhausted participants are removed on progress processing. Completion checks and per-progress hazard loops have a specific ordering; avoid assuming survival and removal happen immediately after each individual hazard.

articles.title: Quest challenges, rewards, and permanent discounts
articles.summary: What specialization markers and quest hazards actually do, including first-clear economics.

sections.title: Quest hazards
paragraphs: Triggered challenges independently roll each whole quest progress tick. Dangerous has the default 5% trigger chance: each participant takes random ordinary damage around (15 + quest difficulty ÷ 50) × (quest difficulty ÷ participant base damage), with a ÷1.3 to ×1.3 range.

Exhausting triggers every progress tick and adds 10% of the normal quest energy cost. Dexterity Energy triggers at the default 5% chance; each participant failing a Dexterity test against raw quest difficulty pays 15 times normal quest energy cost.

Fighter, Rogue, and Mage specialization markers halve effective difficulty for matching archetypes. Cleric specialization quarters it. These alter progress contribution and the low-performance penalty, but Dangerous and Dexterity Energy use the raw quest difficulty. Increase Duration is a descriptive marker; the actual duration formula is the quest’s DurationMultiplier.

sections.title: First and repeat rewards
paragraphs: Currency and item rewards are granted once per completed group, not once per participant. Advancement rewards inspect every group member and change only exact matching class types. First-clear and repeat reward lists can differ.

Currency reward count is rounded after multiplying by the board or dungeon’s CoinLootMultiplier. Item reward count is fixed. Item quality uses the output element’s quality: when above 1, it rolls reward quality × random((1 + element quality) ÷ 2, element quality). The default reward quality is 1.
Each Quest Item Loot and Dungeon Item Loot upgrade contributes +0.1 element quality. It improves the quality of reward items rather than multiplying their declared counts.

sections.title: Permanent economic rewards
paragraphs: Clear Mines first sets the Iron Ore discount flag; the resource cost multiplier becomes 0.25. Each repeat multiplies it by another 0.95: 0.25 × 0.95^repeat counter. Its difficulty is 470, base duration 180, and duration multiplier 1.05.

Forest Evangelism first halves forest-worker cost, with each repeat multiplying by another 0.95: 0.5 × 0.95^repeat counter. It has difficulty 600, base duration 180, duration multiplier 1.05, and the Cleric specialization marker. These discounts multiply other applicable cost calculations.

sections.title: Quest roster
paragraphs: Ordinary quests are Patrol Market, Exterminate Rats, Dispel Library, Clear Mines, Forest Evangelism, and Mercurial Reagents. Eight further quests provide the intermediate class branches. Use each quest’s entity page for exact first/repeat items and research gates.

articles.title: Dungeon runs, stages, loot, and retreat
articles.summary: The five-adventurer expedition loop and what happens between fights.

sections.title: Starting
paragraphs: A dungeon node needs five Adventurer inputs, an available selected dungeon, no active party, and the full supply currency payment. It consumes all five inputs and applies party buffs. Ticks occur every two seconds; this tick interval is fixed in Dungeon.Update rather than divided by the node’s Speed.

Each dungeon has eight stages, alternating nonboss and boss. Stage health = BaseHealth × StageDifficulty. Nightmare endgame adds its own health multiplier. Every active combat tick increments StageTick, then adds random party base damage ÷ 1.2 to ×1.2 to stage progress. Challenges and combat traits execute next.

Ordinary party damage follows: at least one hit occurs, with a 50% continuation chance after each hit. That gives an average two hits but no fixed maximum. Dead/Exhausted members are then removed. Losing the last member records a wipe and resets the run.

sections.title: Damage and boss escalation
paragraphs: Dungeon damage rolls between integer StageDifficulty ÷ 50 and integer StageDifficulty ÷ 33, multiplied by the requested hazard multiplier. On boss stages the multiplier also gains ×(1 + 0.015 × StageTick). This grows every active combat tick, so stalled boss fights become more dangerous.
Normal hits use tank-targeting odds. Individual challenges can bypass armor, target everyone, consume energy, or impose separate skill checks.

sections.title: Loot and between-stage healing
paragraphs: Reaching stage health sets three cooldown ticks before looting. Before granting rewards, all ItemReward outputs for the stage must exist and have no buffered items. A blocked output delays loot and energy payment, then retries.

Successful loot grants every stage reward, deducts the stage EnergyCost from each member (default 10), invokes the stage callback, and increments clear count. After limit-break checks, healing traits and the first full Healer can act. A cleared stage advances when the standard Healer has no eligible wounded target.

The final stage records victory and clears the party before the normal healing phase. Successful expeditions do not output the adventurers. A wipe or victory sets five cooldown ticks and resets stage progress to the beginning.

sections.title: Retreat and extra loot
paragraphs: Retreat refunds each supply currency by the fraction 1 − zero-based CurrentStage ÷ total stages, truncating each refund to an integer. It clears the party and run with two cooldown ticks. Changing dungeon selection mid-run invokes retreat.

Trash Loot upgrades independently give a 5% × upgrade-count chance each nonboss combat tick to award 25% of every Ducat reward on that stage. This explicit 0.25 reward call does not use the node CoinLootMultiplier. Normal stage currency rewards do use the coin multiplier, which grows by 0.1 per coin upgrade.

sections.title: How to read the table
paragraphs: All probabilities are independent per active combat tick when the hazard is listed on the current stage. D means one fresh GetDungeonDamage(1) roll with that stage’s current difficulty and boss escalation. A ×multiplier requests a roll at that multiplier; final armor and traits are applied afterward unless marked armor-ignoring.

Individual difficulty = integer stage difficulty ÷ 4; group difficulty = integer stage difficulty ÷ 3. A group check stops at the first successful member. A random target is selected from current party members.

sections.title: Injected poison
paragraphs: The Inject Poison debuff itself deals 0.2D armor-ignoring damage on each dungeon combat hook. Its tick does not ask for another Poison resistance value. The initial injection avoids adding the debuff whenever the target already has any positive poison reduction. Multiple identical debuffs keep the highest trait quality rather than stacking duplicate active traits.

articles.title: Energy, death, and dungeon limit breaks
articles.summary: What exhaustion removes, how recovery works, and when Faith can prolong an expedition.

sections.title: Health and exhaustion
paragraphs: Health and Energy initialize at full fractions. A combatant is Dead when its health fraction is zero. A character with a positive energy pool is Exhausted at zero energy unless its LimitBreak flag is active. Nonhumans normally have no energy pool, and ordinary humans with zero base Energy ignore Energy equipment.

Energy loss is clamped to the 0–100% fraction. Positive loss passes through energy-loss traits; negative loss restores energy without those modifiers. Healing passes through healing-taken traits and clamps to maximum health. No separate persistent injury-status system is present in these core combatant classes; remaining health is the injury measure.

Quest and training systems remove exhausted participants instead of automatically resting them. Arena only returns living, non-Exhausted eligible humans. War removes soldiers on death. Dungeon parties are consumed by defeat, victory, or retreat rather than sent through a survivor output.

sections.title: Limit Break
paragraphs: With Dungeon Limit Break, a member at zero energy can remain active while other party members still have energy. Its human combat power is reduced to 75%. If the whole party reaches zero energy, the run records a wipe and resets even with Limit Break.

With the Faith-based second limit break, an energy-loss call that reaches zero tries to spend round(requested energy loss × 5) Faith. On success it sets the member to exactly 1 CurrentEnergy. This is not a full refill and is not priced only on the missing portion. It can be invoked by stage costs or challenge losses.

A stage completion deducts energy before CheckForLimitBreak; this check can remove zero-energy members or end a fully exhausted run. Consumables that restore energy during later healing hooks cannot be assumed to rescue members already removed by earlier checks.

sections.title: Completion recovery
paragraphs: ActivityCompleted raises Level, clears temporary buffs, and fully heals full Healers; it does not restore Energy. Potions, energy amulets, and energy scrolls supply explicit recovery effects. Other humans retain their remaining health when returned from training, quest, or arena activities.

articles.title: War Effort combat, medals, and defense
articles.summary: How army power becomes territorial progress and why completed fronts still need soldiers.

sections.title: Army progress
paragraphs: War updates every two seconds. Combine carried PartialProgress with each soldier’s base damage. A human without a main-hand weapon contributes half. Adventurers additionally multiply contribution by lerp(0.5, 1, energy fraction). This energy weighting is separate from zero-energy human power loss.

Enemy strength is interpolated between the current stage’s StartStrength and EndStrength using progress fraction. While accumulated power is strictly greater than current strength, subtract that strength and gain one progress point, recalculating as stages change. Retain the rounded remainder for future updates.

If the update gains no progress points, it loses one instead. Partial progress is still retained. A new conquered stage begins at 5 progress. Losing below zero falls back one stage with progress set to its maximum minus 5; the first stage floors at zero.

sections.title: Defense
paragraphs: After every stage is cleared, the front becomes a defense meter. Required strength uses half the last stage’s EndStrength, except the North keeps full EndStrength. The defense meter can fall back into the final stage if lost. Holding territory is therefore an ongoing supply commitment.
The final defense meter’s base maximum is 100. Nightmare scaling can alter endgame maximum progress. Defense combat uses lower damage-hit and medal chances than active conquest.

sections.title: Damage, healing, medals
paragraphs: Each soldier has a 66% chance per conquest update to be hit, or 33% in completed-front defense. The damage basis interpolates from the previous stage’s EnemyDamage to the current one where applicable, then rolls from that value to ×1.6, truncates to an integer, and uses normal armor/traits. Dead soldiers are removed.

A human carrying any WeaponItemType can generate a medal on a 20% conquest chance, or about 6.67% during defense. Its death adds another medal unit when that armed-human condition is met. The total is rounded after multiplying by the front’s MedalsMultiplier.
Full Healers cast once subject to the one-per-five-soldiers rounded limit, clamped 1–10. War trait hooks then run, including potions, passive regeneration, and other special effects.

sections.title: Inputs and remains
paragraphs: War Effort accepts combatants; Adventurers require the adventurer-to-war technology. Intake continues while that front’s CanProgress condition allows it. The passive recruitment technology gives a separate 5% chance at one Medal per new soldier.

With a remains output present and empty, a soldier death has a 50% chance to create Human Remains carrying the soldier’s quality. This branch is not restricted to human item types by its code. Barracks has base output rate 0.5 × Speed and quality resource cost multiplier 2.

sections.title: All four war fronts
paragraphs: These are base values before active Nightmare scaling. Ironcrag Siege intake is gated by currently holding Siege of Yensburg stage 4. Final defense keeps full last-stage strength in Ironcrag and halves it in other fronts.

articles.title: Adventure potions, auras, scrolls, and rescue effects
articles.summary: Consumable thresholds and unusual equipment behavior that raw stat lists do not explain.

sections.title: Potions and rations
paragraphs: Healing Potion triggers below 33% health and heals 70 × item quality × the wearer’s healing-done multiplier. Greater Healing Potion uses 180. The wearer’s healing-taken traits then apply. Each consumes the Potion slot. They have hooks in war, quest, arena, and dungeon healing.

Energy Potion triggers below 33% energy, restores 40 × quality, and consumes the Potion slot. Regeneration Potion instead heals 6 × quality on every supported hook and is not consumed by that helper. Rations multiply requested training by 1 + 0.25 × quality.

Lifebearer (Amulet of Healing) multiplies healing received by 1 + 0.2 × quality. Lifebloom heals 2 × quality to eligible rolled recipients: 100% chance for self in arena, 50% per quest party member, 80% per dungeon member. Its war chance uses integer 4 ÷ army count; armies above four therefore receive no Lifebloom healing from that hook.

sections.title: Group energy and resistance
paragraphs: Amulet of Energy restores 40 × quality to the party in quest/dungeon hooks when any member is below 30% energy, or when every member is at most 60%. It consumes the wearer’s Amulet. The energy helper’s ordered scan implements these thresholds.
Fire, Shadow, and Poison protection amulets grant their matching group resistance. Triune Shield grants all three only to its wearer. Resistance uses the highest-quality active source.
Fireball Amulet adds 45 × quality × wearer damage multiplier to war PartialProgress on war hooks and dungeon StageProgress on dungeon healing hooks. It does not use a separate attack entity.

sections.title: Scrolls
paragraphs: Healing Scroll triggers below 33% health, heals 220 × quality × wearer healing-done multiplier, and consumes Scroll. Group Healing Scroll heals 80 × quality × wearer healing-done multiplier: it triggers when anyone is below 35% health, or everyone is at most 65%. War recipients use integer 4 ÷ army count as their chance, so larger armies can consume it without healing recipients.

Damage Scroll adds 4 × wearer CombatPower on the fifth active combat tick of each boss stage. The hook does not consume it and does not directly multiply this extra hit by item quality or damage-trait multiplier.

Energy Scroll restores 30 × quality using the same 30% / 60% group-energy thresholds. Its helper removes Amulet rather than Scroll. In this installed implementation it can therefore remove an equipped amulet while retaining the scroll.

sections.title: Divine protection
paragraphs: Pontiff Ring applies DivineProtection as an aura; Martyr Relic supplies DivineProtection2 on its wearer. When pending damage is at least current health, the protection heals maximum health through normal healing and returns zero incoming damage. Martyr Relic removes Trinket.

The ring branch, in dungeon context, removes Pontiff Rings from party members but asks to remove DivineProtection2 buffs rather than DivineProtection. Stored/aura refresh behavior means it should not be described as a guaranteed clean one-charge effect. Its cleanup branch is also dungeon-specific. These are code-observed exceptions, not promises about intended design.

articles.title: Nightmare adventure scaling and final rewards
articles.summary: How repeated endgame victories change Ironcrag Siege and Tomb of Sholrath.

sections.title: Active scaling
paragraphs: When Nightmare is active, Tomb of Sholrath uses these multipliers based on total NightmareCount N: stage difficulty ×(1 + 0.01N), stage health additionally ×(1 + 0.05N), and supply cost ×(1 + 0.1N). Difficulty is rounded first, then health is calculated and cast to a long after the extra health multiplier.

Because stage health already multiplies BaseHealth by the scaled difficulty, effective health grows from both the difficulty and dedicated health factors. Dungeon challenge checks and damage also rise with the scaled difficulty.

Ironcrag Siege is the endgame war. While Nightmare is active, its maximum progress uses ×(1 + 0.05N); enemy strength and damage use ×(1 + 0.01N). Its stage-completion branch still compares progress to the stage’s declared ProgressAmount, so do not interpret the scaled MaxProgress property as an unconditional replacement of every completion threshold.

sections.title: Reward readiness
paragraphs: Fragmented Nightmare rewards are ready while Nightmare is active, or for the very first victory when NightmareCount is zero. Their base reward is two items.

Distilled Nightmare is ready for the first victory regardless of activity state, or afterward when Nightmare is active and NightmareProgress exceeds 0.99. When ready it increases NightmareCount by one and subtracts one progress only if progress is at least 1.

A Distilled Nightmare reward resets Ironcrag’s final hold: a completed front is moved back to zero-based stage 3, and that stage’s progress is set to 10. The Tomb’s current availability requirement is final Ironcrag completion, so another attempt depends on restoring that war condition.
The first ready Distilled reward also opens the game’s victory popup. Reaching the last boss is therefore distinct from qualifying for every repeat reward.

related.label: Dungeon runs, stages, loot, and retreat

articles.title: Production simulation and bottlenecks
articles.summary: How diagrams, pipes, queues, and blocked outputs determine actual throughput.

sections.title: Simulation order
paragraphs: The production manager advances the player with Unity's frame delta. Every saved flow diagram is updated, so changing the displayed diagram does not suspend the others. Within each diagram, all buildings update in list order and then all pipes update in list order.

This is a frame-driven simulation, not a universal once-per-second production tick. Buildings implement their own timers. A nominal items-per-second rate can be limited by frame updates because many building Update methods finish at most one operation per call.

sections.title: Pipes and buffers
paragraphs: Pipes repeatedly transfer the first available output item while the receiving input accepts its type and has buffer space. There is no pipe travel-time or pipe-length penalty in the transfer method. Items remain individual inventory objects with their quality, equipment, and character data.

An input's acceptance filter and its capacity are separate checks. An unacceptable first item marks the pipe as rejected and blocks the queue behind it. A full but otherwise compatible destination simply stalls transfer. Most utility inputs and outputs hold one item; resource outputs normally hold five; recipe inputs hold exactly that reagent's required count.

sections.title: Diagnosing a stopped chain
paragraphs: Check the destination's item filter, its input capacity, all output capacities of a multi-output recipe, the building's currency cost, automatic worker, and any shared resource quota or war gate. A craft can wait with its ingredients already consumed until every required output has room.

Recipe completion checks whether each output has at least one free place, then adds the entire result batch. A large batch may therefore exceed its nominal buffer size. These are queue limits, not an item stack system.

related.label: Saves, autosaves, pause, and offline behavior
Quest challenges, rewards, and permanent discounts
War Effort combat, medals, and defense

articles.title: Resource quotas and harvesting
articles.summary: The shared capacity rules behind mines, suppliers, farms, and recruitment.

sections.title: Quota is shared production capacity
paragraphs: Each resource has a global available quota. Approximately every 0.1 seconds the player totals the desired output of every matching resource building in every diagram. If demand exceeds quota, all those buildings receive the same multiplier: quota divided by total demand. Otherwise the multiplier is 1.

Desired output is zero when a resource building has no queued work or its normal progress is already at least 1. A completed building waiting for output space stops requesting further normal progress. Quota utilization shown in the interface averages recorded demand samples.

sections.title: Production and payment
paragraphs: A resource building queues and pays for a normal item before producing it. An automatic Worker queues a new order when the normal queue becomes empty; manual clicks can queue up to five paid orders. Failed payment leaves the order unqueued.

Actual progress per second is building OutputPerSecond multiplied by the resource quota multiplier. Most resource buildings start at 1 × Speed items per second; Barracks and Adventurers Guild use 0.5 × Speed. Output is blocked when its five-place buffer is full.

sections.title: Bonus output and quality
paragraphs: Productivity advances a separate counter using the same quota-adjusted production progress. When the bonus counter reaches 1, the next available output consumes bonus progress instead of normal progress or a paid queued order.
Resource quality is sampled between square root of building Quality and building Quality. Human recruits also receive the Human Quality prestige bonus before their character data is initialized.

sections.title: Quota upgrades
paragraphs: A quota upgrade adds the resource's configured QuotaAmount. Its price is QuotaBaseCost multiplied by the resource's quota growth factor raised to the number of previous quota upgrades. Resource Cost Reduction prestige reduces only the amount above 1 in that growth factor.

The iron-ore quest discount multiplies quota upgrade prices by 0.25 × 0.95 raised to the repeat discount counter. Resource Artisan variants add a gold surcharge per normal order: resource value × 0.2 per upgrade for ordinary resources, or × 2 per upgrade for recruits.

related.label: Quest challenges, rewards, and permanent discounts
War Effort combat, medals, and defense

articles.title: Mines and supply depots
articles.summary: Choosing raw materials and paying for resource orders.

sections.title: Mine
paragraphs: A Mine accepts resource selections tagged Mine. Its displayed name changes for iron ore, sapphire, gold ore, and silver ore. The first Mine is free; later Mines use the normal Resource building price escalation.
A Mine shares its resource's quota with all other buildings producing that resource. Building more Mines cannot by itself raise the global quota.

sections.title: Supply Depot and Adventure Supplies
paragraphs: Supply Depot selects resources tagged Supply and is purchased with Gold. Adventure Supplies selects resources tagged AdventureSupplies and is purchased with Gold and Rings. Both use the standard ResourceElement order, quota, five-item output, quality, and productivity systems.
Resource selection is restricted to the currently available resources. Quota must be positive for ordinary resources to appear in that list; unlocked farm resources are a special exception.

related.label: Quest challenges, rewards, and permanent discounts
War Effort combat, medals, and defense

articles.title: Forests and forest crews
articles.summary: Crew allocation, harvest capacity, and workforce costs.

sections.title: Crew roles and war gate
paragraphs: The forest workforce has Unassigned, Forager, Logger, and Hunter roles. Assigning workers to an active role consumes the same number of unassigned workers; removing them returns that number to the unassigned pool.

Harvesting is blocked until forest war stage 1. Each forest resource defines its worker role and WorkersPerItem requirement. Forest buildings requesting the same role compete for that role's assigned crew.

sections.title: Capacity formula
paragraphs: For each role, desired workforce is the sum of each active forest's desired items per second × that resource's WorkersPerItem. If demand is above assigned workers, the production multiplier is assigned workers divided by demand. Otherwise it is 1. Actual building output is Speed × that role multiplier.

Forest orders are paid when queued and have the same five-order manual queue, separate productivity counter, and five-item output buffer as ordinary resource buildings. Quality is sampled between square root of Quality and Quality. Each Forest Artisan adds 20% of resource value in extra gold to each paid order.

sections.title: Buying workers
paragraphs: Base worker price is 12 Requisition and 12 Medals. The price multiplier grows by 1.08 raised to total workers, including unassigned workers. Resource Cost Reduction prestige reduces the growth above 1.
The forest-worker quest discount multiplies price by 0.5 × 0.95 raised to its repeat counter. Forest Workforce technology supplies an additional ×0.5 multiplier.

related.label: Quest challenges, rewards, and permanent discounts

articles.title: Farming and field expansion
articles.summary: Plots establish farm capacity; farm buildings harvest that capacity.

sections.title: Fields and quota
paragraphs: The field begins 3 columns wide and 2 rows high. Each cell can hold a selected unlocked farm resource. Every matching planted cell contributes that resource's configured PlotYield to its global production quota.

Farms are blocked until eastern war stage 1. Field quota is zero while blocked, and Farm buildings separately check the same war gate approximately once per second. A planted field establishes available capacity; a Farm building still queues and pays for harvested items.

sections.title: Expansion costs
paragraphs: A field expansion is priced from 12 Rings and 12 Crowns multiplied by a sum of escalating terms. UpgradeCount is current width + current height − 5. For a request of n new plots, the multiplier is the sum of growth^(UpgradeCount + i), for i from 0 through n − 1.
The normal growth is 1.2. Resource Cost Reduction prestige reduces the amount of that growth above 1. The farm data declares a maximum width of 6; field dimensions and selected cells are saved.

sections.title: Farm output
paragraphs: Each Farm is a standard ResourceElement tagged Farm, with a base desired speed of 1 × Speed while its war gate is open. All Farms harvesting the same crop share the crop quota. Farm Artisan quality and extra order cost follow the resource rules.

articles.title: Crafting, recipes, and automatic work
articles.summary: When ingredients are consumed, how long crafting takes, and what causes blocked crafts.

sections.title: Starting a craft
paragraphs: Each recipe declares reagent slots, counts, optional currency cost, result slots, and an unlock technology. The building must support the recipe's tag and the recipe technology must be purchased.

When no craft is running, a recipe building checks that every reagent input has its full required count. It then pays the recipe's currency cost and removes those items into a persistent CraftingInput. This starts a craft even without an automatic Worker; the Worker controls automatic progress, while manual clicks can progress a started craft.

sections.title: Timing
paragraphs: Unless explicitly set, recipe crafting time is (1.5 + 0.5 × total reagent item count) × CraftingTimeMultiplier seconds. Automatic progress per second is Speed divided by CraftingTime. Normal completion resets the running input, after which another ready craft can begin.

Every recipe output must have room before results are created. This includes an output for an unchanged or transformed input character as well as ordinary items. Recipes with probabilistic results use a single shared output and choose one result by the configured weights.

sections.title: Value
paragraphs: A recipe's default base value starts with the base values of value-affecting explicit reagents plus the gold equivalents of currency costs when CostIncreasesValue is enabled. The normal value multiplier is 1 + 0.15 × number of reagent slots + 0.15 if qualifying currency costs exist + 0.025 × CraftingTime; an explicit ValueMultiplier replaces it.

Filter-based reagents use preview items for the interface but default to not contributing preview value or input quality. Currency rewards are rolled at output quality, rounded, and credited when the craft completes.

articles.title: Crafting workshops and their roles
articles.summary: The recipe stations and the shared rules they use.

sections.title: Station families
paragraphs: Forge, Blacksmith, Tailor, Leatherworker, Carpenter, Engraver, Campfire, Enchanter, Butcher, Kitchen, Jeweler, Summoning Circle, Alchemist, Inventor, Scribe, Shrine, Graveyard, and Necromancer all derive from RecipeElement. Their recipes use the shared timing, input quality, manual crafting, worker, and output-blocking rules.

Each station normally offers only its own RecipeTag. The Kitchen is the exception: its recipe menu also offers Campfire recipes, and its computed Speed is doubled after upgrades. This makes it a faster replacement for campfire cooking as well as the station for kitchen-specific meals.

sections.title: Purchase currencies
paragraphs: Forge and Blacksmith use Gold. Tailor, Leatherworker, and Carpenter use Gold and Requisition. Campfire and Engraver use Gold and Medals. Enchanter, Butcher, and Kitchen use Gold and Rings. Jeweler, Summoning Circle, Alchemist, Inventor, Scribe, Shrine, Graveyard, and Necromancer use Gold and Ducats.
The first Forge is free. Crafting stations are stackable; stacking increases Speed, while individual recipe unlocks and per-craft currency costs remain relevant.

articles.title: Item quality and critical crafting
articles.summary: How ingredient quality, artisans, equipment rolls, and critical crafts interact.

sections.title: Craft quality formula
paragraphs: Let A be the average quality of all input items whose reagent slots affect quality; use A = 1 if none qualify. Let B be the building's Quality stat. Set H = B + A − 1. If H < 1, output quality is exactly H. Otherwise output quality is sampled from (A + H)/2 through H.

For example, average ingredient quality 1.20 and building Quality 1.10 give an output range of 1.25 to 1.30. A plain building with B = 1 preserves uniform ingredient quality. New equipment additionally receives the Equipment Quality prestige bonus.

sections.title: Critical craft
paragraphs: With Critical Craft technology, each output quality roll has a 1% chance to add its rolled distance above the minimum a second time. A critical craft is not simply a flat quality multiplier and does nothing when the roll equals the minimum.
Inventory quality values less than 0.01 away from 1 are snapped to exactly 1. Ordinary item sell value is rounded BaseValue × Quality; equipment adds the sell values of its enhancements.

sections.title: Equipment stat rolls
paragraphs: Each equipment base stat rolls from floor(base stat × 0.9 × item quality) up to, but excluding, ceil(base stat × 1.1 × item quality), unless both bounds are equal. Updating quality clears and rerolls these base equipment stats, so a Refiner or quality enhancement can change the rolls as well as the quality number.

Artisan upgrades add 0.1 to building Quality per copy. Ordinary crafting Artisans also add 10% of the recipe base value per upgrade to per-craft costs, converted into each existing cost currency; recipes without an existing currency cost get a gold surcharge.

related.label: Equipment slots, hands, and armor affinity

articles.title: Productivity and handcrafting
articles.summary: Bonus progress produces extra results without spending another set of ingredients.

sections.title: How bonus crafts work
paragraphs: Overseer grants 0.1 Productivity per installed upgrade. A recipe adds its BaseProductivity and clamps the final result to at least zero. During normal automatic progress, a separate productivity meter gains normal progress × Productivity; equipment recipes gain half that amount.

If productivity reaches 1, a completion uses one productivity point while keeping the current normal craft and its original ingredients. A subsequent normal completion consumes the running craft. This produces bonus batches without a fresh reagent set or another start payment.

Recipes with enhancement results explicitly disable productivity progress. Many character transformation, prayer, burial, or special chance recipes set BaseProductivity to −999, which suppresses ordinary building upgrade productivity after clamping. Manual Handcrafting Productivity prestige is added after that clamp, so it can still accrue bonus progress on such recipes unless enhancement output explicitly disables it.

sections.title: Manual crafting
paragraphs: A manual click on a running recipe adds Speed ÷ CraftingTime ÷ 2.5 to normal progress. Equivalently, each click supplies 0.4 seconds of work at the building's current speed. Clicking is available only while a craft exists and its normal progress is below 1.

Manual productivity uses the final building Productivity plus Handcrafting Productivity prestige, multiplied by the manual progress amount and halved for equipment. Because the prestige bonus is added after the recipe's negative BaseProductivity has already been clamped to zero, a −999 BaseProductivity recipe can still gain manual bonus progress. Enhancement recipes retain their explicit disable check. Manual resource clicks work differently: they purchase queued orders rather than directly adding recipe progress.

sections.title: Practical consequences
paragraphs: Faster workers and stacking produce normal and productivity progress faster, but cannot remove a resource quota bottleneck or full output. A bonus result still requires free output capacity.

The automatic recipe productivity meter only accrues while below 1, and completion creates at most one batch per building update. Frame timing and blocking can therefore affect throughput around very fast or high-productivity setups.

articles.title: Workers, upgrades, stacking, and refunds
articles.summary: The common upgrade system used by production and service buildings.

sections.title: Worker and speed
paragraphs: The first Worker enables CanAutoCraft and adds no speed bonus. Each additional Worker of that exact type adds 0.5 Speed. Speed bonuses add to a base of 1, then the result is multiplied by StackSize.

Repeat Workers are permitted on resource buildings, recipe buildings, Shops, Forests, Training Grounds, and Disenchanters. Other building types normally allow only one Worker. Some services, including Inn, Luxury Shop, and Mercenary Guild, are intrinsically automatic.

sections.title: Upgrade slots and costs
paragraphs: Technology grants upgrade slots and the set of available upgrades separately for each building type. Upgrade effects are recalculated from the installed upgrades. The nth copy of a particular upgrade type is counted independently of other types.

The shared upgrade price uses a base of 858, the upgrade's CostMultiplier, and a ×1.5 price factor for each existing upgrade of the same exact type. Its cost tier is the larger of the upgrade's minimum tier and building cost tier plus that existing count. Currency conversion, rounding, and deterministic identifier variation also affect the displayed price.

sections.title: Stacking and construction prices
paragraphs: The base building price uses 780 and its configured CostMultiplier. Repeated Resource buildings use a 1.04 count multiplier, Crafting buildings 1.02, and Consumption buildings 1.10. Utility buildings use 1.00. Counts include stack sizes across all diagrams.

The declared maximum stack size is five. Stackable families include resources, forests, recipes, and Shops. Stacking multiplies computed Speed; it does not automatically enlarge their IO buffers or a Shop's gold capacity.

sections.title: Refunds and artisans
paragraphs: Building refunds are half the previous-count purchase price plus half-price refunds for installed upgrades, with repeated upgrades accounted for by type. Copy prices include the copied stack and installed upgrades.

Artisans add 0.1 Quality, with the ordinary Artisan availability requiring forest war stage 2. Training Artisan also subtracts 0.2 Speed per copy. Resource Artisan variants apply the resource-specific extra production costs described on the resource pages.

articles.title: Shops and gold collection
articles.summary: Shops sell suitable items immediately into a local till, then require collection.

sections.title: What Shops accept
paragraphs: A Shop accepts any sellable item with positive SellValue except CombatantItemType. Its one-item input is consumed whenever the till is below capacity; item sale itself has no per-item crafting timer.
Sale gold is rounded SellValue × (1 + 0.05 × Cashier count), then multiplied by 1 + Sell Value prestige when that bonus is positive. The last five sales are retained for its tooltip.

sections.title: Capacity and collection
paragraphs: Base gold capacity is 10,000, increased to 50,000 with Shop Expansion. Coffers multiply that base capacity by 1 + 2 × Coffers count. A sale can take the till above its cap because capacity is checked before the whole item value is added.

Manual collection transfers the smaller of stored gold and capacity. Overflow from a very valuable sale stays in the till for another collection. A Worker collects every 10 ÷ Speed seconds; extra workers and stacks improve that collection interval.
The first Shop is free. StackSize changes computed Speed, while capacity is based on GoldCap and Coffers count rather than stack size.

articles.title: Luxury Shops and crown chances
articles.summary: Quality goods can produce enhanced gold income and occasional Crowns.

sections.title: Eligible items
paragraphs: Luxury Shop is intrinsically automatic. It accepts positive-value, sellable noncombatants only when item Quality is strictly greater than 1. It consumes one buffered item each update and credits proceeds directly.
Gold before rounding equals item SellValue × item Quality. If Quality − 1 is strictly above 0.2, multiply that by 1.2. Sell Value prestige then multiplies it by 1 + its bonus.

sections.title: Crown roll
paragraphs: Food never generates Crowns here. For other eligible goods, Quality − 1 must be strictly greater than 0.1 before any Crown roll occurs. The chance is clamp(Quality − 1, 0, 0.5). On success, Crown quantity is the integer part of the pre-rounded gold value divided by 2,400.

A successful roll can still award zero Crowns if the sale value is below one Crown's gold equivalent. The Crown check does not reduce the gold payout. Quality 1.10 or 1.20 sits on a strict threshold rather than automatically receiving the higher-tier effect.

articles.title: Requisition Offices and contracts
articles.summary: Convert selected equipment types into Requisition using base value.

sections.title: Contract deliveries
paragraphs: An office selects an index from the player's shared list of contracted item types and accepts exactly that type. It adds integer(BaseValue × (1 + 0.1 × Req Cashier count)) to StoredValue for each item consumed.

The code uses item.Type.BaseValue, so item quality and added enhancement sell value do not increase delivery credit. Every 1,000 StoredValue converts into one Requisition, with the remainder retained as progress.

sections.title: Capacity, workers, and passive generation
paragraphs: Stored Requisition capacity is 10 × (1 + 2 × Coffers count). Reaching capacity stops the update before passive progress and deliveries. A completion can go above capacity because generated Requisition is added as a batch.

Without a Worker, generated Requisition remains local until collected. With a Worker, new Requisition and any pending local collection are credited immediately. Installing an automatic worker also collects an existing local balance.
Each Req Passive upgrade adds 0.02 Requisition worth of stored value per one-second tick: 20 StoredValue per second at the normal 1,000 gold equivalent, or one Requisition every 50 seconds.

sections.title: Contract generation and reroll cost
paragraphs: The first generated contract is randomly iron sword or iron dagger. The second is simple robe, rough vest, or softwood bow. Later candidates come from available recipe results that are EquipmentItemType; already contracted types are removed while more than one candidate remains.

Fallbacks for missing random candidates are mushroom stew for contract 3, wild staff for 4, arcanium sword for 5, and iron sword afterwards. Reroll cost spends all current Requisition if below five; otherwise it is max(5, current Requisition integer-divided by 100).

articles.title: Disenchanting and mana production
articles.summary: Equipment converts into mana, with quality and enhancement adjustments.

sections.title: Eligible equipment and timing
paragraphs: A Disenchanter accepts positive-value, sellable EquipmentItemType except Food, Potion, and Scroll slots. The declared 1.04 quality constant is not used as an acceptance gate: low-quality equipment is accepted with a payout penalty.

An item takes 1 ÷ Speed seconds to process. Mana is stored locally, with no capacity check in this class. A Worker collects whenever the local balance is positive; manual collection transfers all stored Mana.

sections.title: Mana formula
paragraphs: Start with SellValue and a conversion multiplier of 0.9 ÷ 11. If item Quality is below 1.04, multiply by 0.75. For equipment without any enhancement, multiply by another 0.75. If it has an Enchant enhancement, subtract half that enhancement's sell value from the value being converted.

Item ManaValue is the ceiling of adjusted value × conversion multiplier. The Disenchanter then rounds ManaValue × (1 + 0.1 × Mana Cashier count). Each Mana Passive upgrade adds three local Mana per second regardless of item supply.
An ordinary quality-1 unenhanced item receives both 0.75 penalties. Enhancements and base quality are separate tests; a Blessing or Engraving is enough to avoid the no-enhancement penalty.

articles.title: Restaurants, food, and Crowns
articles.summary: Meals generate Gold and probabilistic Crown income.

sections.title: Food sales
paragraphs: A Restaurant accepts sellable, positive-value equipment in the Food slot. A sale starts with V = SellValue × (1 + 0.05 × Cashier count). If the food has any enhancement, V is multiplied by 1.2.

Crown score is V ÷ 2,400 × (1 + 0.1 × Restaurant Crowns count). Halve that score when the food's default recipe is missing or is not tagged Kitchen; this includes Campfire foods even when made inside a Kitchen.

sections.title: How Crown score resolves
paragraphs: While the remaining score is positive, the game tests a random chance equal to that score, awarding one Crown and subtracting one on success. Scores of at least 1 therefore guarantee their whole-number portion and roll the fractional remainder.

If item Quality is strictly greater than 1.2, the gold value receives a Big Tippers multiplier of 1 + min(0.5, 0.5 × Big Tippers count × (Quality − 0.8)). This bonus is applied after the Crown score is calculated.
If at least one Crown was won, gold value is halved. The final gold amount is rounded and both rewards are stored locally. Restaurant does not read Sell Value prestige in its sale code.

sections.title: Collection
paragraphs: A Worker collects both currencies every 10 ÷ Speed seconds. Manual collection also takes both balances, though the manual-availability check requires stored Gold greater than zero. There is no local storage cap in Restaurant's code.

articles.title: Currencies and the exchange
articles.summary: Gold equivalents, eligible currencies, taxes, and rounding.

sections.title: Gold equivalents
paragraphs: Currencies have fixed gold equivalents used for conversion and prices: Gold 1, Requisition 1,000, Medal 600, Ring 1,200, Mana 11, Crown 2,400, Ducat 5,200, Ingenuity 200, and Faith 100.
Mana, Ingenuity, and Faith are explicitly nontradeable. The currency interface exposes exchange on tradeable non-Gold currencies after Currency Exchange technology is owned.

sections.title: Tax formula
paragraphs: Base exchange tax is 1, meaning 100%. Currency Exchange Tax technology halves it to 0.5. Currency Tax Reduction prestige further multiplies tax by 1 minus its current bonus.

Buying N units costs trunc(N × gold equivalent × (1 + tax)) Gold. Selling N units receives trunc(N × gold equivalent ÷ (1 + tax)) Gold. The buy and sell formulas use opposite sides of the same multiplier, so a round trip loses value.

sections.title: Example and accounting
paragraphs: At the base 100% tax, one Requisition costs 2,000 Gold to buy and sells for 500 Gold. At 50% tax it costs 1,500 and sells for 666 after truncation.

Exchange credits use isIncome = false, unlike normal production rewards. The purchase slider's maximum is floor(available Gold ÷ taxed unit price). Currency unlocks come from their associated production or progression technology.

related.label: Quest challenges, rewards, and permanent discounts
War Effort combat, medals, and defense

articles.title: Refining and destruction risk
articles.summary: A Refiner trades items and optional Mana for incremental quality.

sections.title: Cycle and eligibility
paragraphs: A Refiner processes a buffered item in three seconds and requires its output slot to be free before resolving. Its cycle does not use the building's Speed. Failure consumes the item permanently; success returns the same item with higher quality.

Without the appropriate Mana technology mode, combatants are rejected. With Mana mode and Refiner Demon, nonhuman combatants become eligible; Refiner Human allows all items while Mana mode is active. Refiner Mana defaults Mana use on for newly created refiners unless a copied preference overrides it.

sections.title: Failure and Mana formulas
paragraphs: Without Mana, failure chance is min(max(Quality − 1, 0.25) × human factor, 0.95), where the human factor is 2 for HumanItemType and 1 otherwise. With Mana the max(...) value is divided by four before the human factor and 95% cap.

Mana cost is round(SellValue × 0.25 ÷ 11). If payment fails, the item still resolves using the non-Mana failure chance. At quality 1, ordinary items fail 25% without Mana or 6.25% with paid Mana; humans fail 50% or 12.5%.

sections.title: Success
paragraphs: A successful refine adds a random 0.05 to 0.10 quality. Critical Craft technology adds an independent 1% chance to double that increase. Increasing quality rerolls base equipment stats through SetQuality.
The Refiner uses no automatic Worker check. Connecting a loop can repeatedly refine the same item, but its failure probability generally rises with quality and eventually reaches the cap.

related.label: Equipment slots, hands, and armor affinity

articles.title: Enchanting, engraving, and blessings
articles.summary: Enhancement slots, eligible inputs, and preservation of the original equipment.

sections.title: Slots and restrictions
paragraphs: Enhancements are stored by EnhancementType. Before Enhance Multiple technology, any existing enhancement blocks another enhancement. After the technology, the item may receive one of each enhancement type, but cannot receive a second of the same type.

Engraver recipes distinguish heavy armor, light or medium armor, weapons, and jewelry. Enchanter recipes use filters for weapons, shields, armor, food, and other recipe-specific targets. Shrine blessings distinguish weapons from nonweapon equipment. A valid item must also pass CanEnhance for that enhancement type.

sections.title: Applying an enhancement
paragraphs: An enhancement recipe returns the original item from reagent slot zero and adds an ItemEnhancementData object whose quality is the craft's rolled output quality. This preserves the item's identity and existing data.

For enhancements with AddQuality, the base item receives that fixed bonus plus a random value between (enhancement quality − 1)/2 and enhancement quality − 1. The item-quality enchant also adds Dark Essence Quality prestige to the fixed increase.

Enhancement result recipes disable bonus productivity progress, even though Overseer may be available in their upgrade list. New material recipes at the same stations still use their own recipe's normal productivity rules.

sections.title: Value and equipment
paragraphs: Equipment SellValue is its normal rounded base value × quality plus every enhancement's sell value. Enhancement stats are added to the equipment's base rolled stats. Filling all enhancement slots triggers the Full Enhance achievement.

related.label: Equipment slots, hands, and armor affinity

articles.title: Collectors, Distributors, and Manifolds
articles.summary: Different merging and splitting tools have different priority behavior.

sections.title: Collector
paragraphs: Collector begins with two inputs and one output, each buffered for one item. If the output has room, it tries the current input; after a transfer or an empty attempt it advances to the next connected input.

It skips disconnected inputs when advancing, but tries only the selected input in a single update. An empty selected input therefore costs an update before another input is tried. Additional inputs can be added; collapse removes only disconnected trailing slots while keeping at least two.

sections.title: Distributor
paragraphs: Distributor begins with one input and two outputs. It sends one item to the current output and advances to the next connected output. If the selected output is full, it advances and returns for that update.

Distributor skips disconnected outputs when advancing, but does not inspect the downstream item's filter before placing an item into an output buffer. An incompatible item can thus occupy that branch and stall it. Additional outputs are supported; collapse retains at least two.

sections.title: Manifold
paragraphs: Manifold has matching numbers of inputs and outputs, starting at two each. It scans inputs from the first slot and outputs from the first slot, sending one waiting item to the first connected output with buffer space, then returns.

Unlike the rotating Collector and Distributor, this is fixed input and output priority. A continuously supplied early input can take precedence over later inputs. Downstream compatibility is handled by pipes after the transfer, so filters still matter.

articles.title: Filters, Appraisers, Inspectors, and Accountants
articles.summary: Sort by type, statistics, or the kingdom's current currency balance.

sections.title: Filter
paragraphs: Filter has one generic input and two outputs. An exact match to the chosen ItemType goes to output zero; everything else goes to output one. Only the matching route's capacity is checked, so a blocked selected branch stalls that item instead of falling back.
With no chosen type, ordinary input items all go to the nonmatching output. Setting the filter also gives the first output that item's preview type.

sections.title: Appraiser
paragraphs: Appraiser evaluates one selected AppraiserStat and a threshold with Equal, Not Equal, Less Than, Less Than or Equal, Greater Than, or Greater Than or Equal. Passing items go to the first output; failures to the second.
