With no selected stat every item passes. Ordinary items report Quality and Training as round(Quality × 100), and zero for unsupported statistics; specialized item types can override the statistic calculation.

sections.title: Accountant
paragraphs: Accountant releases an item only when its currency comparison passes. It supports the same six comparison operators. It does not charge or reserve the tested currency, so the condition is a gate based on the player's current balance.
Gold balances are integer-divided by 10,000 before comparison. The threshold therefore uses groups of 10,000 Gold. With no selected currency, items pass freely.

sections.title: Inspector
paragraphs: Inspector passes the actual inventory item onward, stores a clone as LastItem for inspection, and keeps a LiveItem reference to the actual object. It does not modify the item's quality or equipment. All these tools use one-item buffers and require their relevant output to have space.

articles.title: Stockpiles and overflow
articles.summary: Local first-in, first-out storage smooths variable production.

sections.title: Storage and output
paragraphs: A Stockpile has a one-item input, one-item main output, and an internal FIFO list with default capacity 10. Each update it accepts one input item if the internal list has room, then moves the oldest stored item into the main output if that output has room.

The input and output buffers are outside the internal Contents count. Consequently a full ten-item internal list is not the entire number of items the node can hold. Mixed item types are allowed and retain insertion order.

sections.title: Overflow behavior
paragraphs: Stockpile Overflow adds a second output. When that output is connected and free, an input item is waiting, and the internal list is at least capacity, the node sends the oldest stored item to overflow first. It then admits the waiting input item.

Overflow therefore releases an older stored item, not the newest arriving item. A full stockpile with no incoming item does not automatically drain through overflow. Main output continues to use the oldest remaining item.

sections.title: Capacity controls
paragraphs: Stockpile Capacity technology enables the capacity slider. Adjusting it changes the internal Capacity integer; the value is copied and saved. Reducing the capacity does not immediately delete existing Contents.

articles.title: Armories and shared item storage
articles.summary: Storage terminals share inventories by item type and channel across diagrams.

sections.title: Input and output terminals
paragraphs: An Armory terminal configured without OutputType accepts compatible incoming items into the player's shared ArmoryContents. A terminal configured with an OutputType requests that item type from shared storage and buffers it for its pipe.

Stored inventory is indexed by channel and exact ItemType, with eight channels. Capacity checks apply to a particular item type in a channel rather than to a building's total inventory. Multiple terminals on that channel access the same pool across diagrams.

sections.title: Costs and dispatch
paragraphs: Armory-family input costs are paid when items enter storage. Ordinary base input cost is 100 Gold, reduced to half by Armory Storage Cost technology. Guildhouse uses a base of 200 Gold; Hoard uses zero.

Stored items are retrieved in FIFO order. Empty output terminals join a waiting queue; an incoming item can be delivered directly into the earliest queued output. Empty requesters briefly wait 0.2 seconds before polling again.

With Armory Overflow technology, an input terminal can pass its waiting item to a connected overflow output when that item's shared capacity is full. Insufficient input fee alone does not trigger overflow because the overflow condition specifically tests storage capacity.

sections.title: Storage families
paragraphs: Armory accepts weapons, headgear, and chest armor, with capacity 10 per type and channel. Pantry accepts Food and Potions and keeps capacity 10. Library accepts Scrolls with capacity 5. Treasury accepts Rings, Amulets, and Trinkets with capacity 5.

Guildhouse accepts Adventurers, or all HumanItemType after Guildhouse Conscripts, with capacity 5. Hoard accepts dungeon-sourced items and noncombatant quest-sourced items with capacity 80, has no input fee, and has no channel-unlock technology requirement.

sections.title: Editing terminals
paragraphs: Opening the relevant storage popup pauses that specific terminal's processing. When an output terminal changes selected item type, any mismatched item already in its output is returned to shared storage.

articles.title: Portals and shared channels
articles.summary: Move arbitrary items between diagrams using Mana-funded storage lanes.

sections.title: Channel storage
paragraphs: Portals use a shared inventory indexed by eight channels and eight channel indices, giving 64 separate lanes. Each lane holds up to 20 items in FIFO order and can contain mixed item types.

A Portal is either an input terminal or an output terminal. Input accepts any item if its one-item buffer is free, then pays Mana to store it in the selected lane. Output requests and forwards the oldest item in that lane.

sections.title: Fees and overflow
paragraphs: The base input fee is 12 Mana per item, reduced to 6 by Portal Cost Reduce and to 3 by Portal Cost Reduce 2. The fee is charged once on entry; the output has no additional fee.

Portal Overflow gives an input a passthrough output. It forwards the waiting item only when the selected lane is full and the overflow output is connected and free. Running out of Mana does not by itself qualify for overflow.

sections.title: Waiting outputs and settings
paragraphs: Empty output terminals join a waiting queue. A newly stored item can be handed directly to the first queued output rather than remaining in the lane's list. Empty polling uses a 0.2-second timeout.
The terminal pauses while its settings popup is active. Changing between input and output clears the previous IO layout. Channel, channel index, direction, and last displayed item are saved.

articles.title: Track switches, timers, and release buttons
articles.summary: Control when individual items enter a chain.

sections.title: Track Switch
paragraphs: With SwitchPosition true, Track Switch passes its waiting item to the first output when there is room. With the switch false, it stops the item unless Track Switch 2 has added a second output and that second output is connected and free.
A full selected route causes a stall; the node does not automatically use the other route. Switch position is copied and saved.

sections.title: Timer
paragraphs: Timer starts with a two-second interval and a two-second countdown. It counts down even when no item is present. Once the countdown has expired and its output is free, it forwards one waiting item and resets the countdown.

It therefore enforces spacing between successful releases rather than imposing a fresh delay starting at each arrival. An item arriving after a long idle can pass immediately. Timer processing does not use Speed or Worker.
The timer settings popup is gated by Outfitter Timeout technology. Its slider sets MaxTime and resets TimeLeft to the same value.

sections.title: Single Button
paragraphs: Single Button spends one queued click only when it successfully transfers an input item to its output. Clicking can queue up to ten releases through the interface. Unused clicks persist when no input is available or output is blocked.

articles.title: Outfitters and equipment automation
articles.summary: Pair humans with compatible equipment and return the equipped character.

sections.title: Inputs and fitting
paragraphs: An Outfitter takes one HumanItemType and one EquipmentItemType. Its input filters check equipment compatibility against the other waiting input when present. Outfitter Skip Replace technology influences whether occupied slots may be replaced.

When both inputs are present, the node examines conflicting equipment. If any conflicting equipped item has the exact same item type as the incoming equipment, it forwards the human unchanged and keeps the incoming equipment available for another character.
Otherwise it consumes both into CurrentHuman and CurrentEquip and calls AddEquipment on the human. Completion returns that human after progress reaches 1 at Speed progress per second.

sections.title: Manual approval and automation
paragraphs: Without Outfitter Automation, an unqueued fitting stops at 80% progress until manually released by its interface. Automation allows it to continue past that point without the queued release.
This setting is a separate technology check, not the generic Worker-derived CanAutoCraft. Output space is required before any fitting work proceeds.

sections.title: Timeout
paragraphs: When a human is waiting without equipment and Timeout is greater than zero, the Outfitter accumulates a timeout and forwards the unchanged human after it is exceeded. The timeout resets when a fitting begins or neither relevant wait condition applies.
Timeout value is copied and saved. Routing humans with incompatible equipment can reject the pipe, so mixed equipment lines benefit from filtering by slot or character eligibility.

articles.title: Inns, healing, and food
articles.summary: Five guests can heal automatically, with optional food accelerating their stay.

sections.title: Guests and timing
paragraphs: Inn is intrinsically automatic and contains five guest slots. Its human input and output each buffer five items. A stay normally has 20 ticks, and all guests advance on a shared two-second timer.

Each tick restores 0.05 Health01, clamped to full health, and removes one remaining tick. A full stay can therefore restore 100% of maximum health. This class does not use Speed to shorten its two-second timer.

sections.title: Food
paragraphs: Inn Add Food enables a second input that accepts Food-slot equipment. A waiting food item is assigned to the first occupied guest slot without food.

With food, each shared tick removes a second remaining tick and restores another 0.05 Health01, halving a complete stay to about ten ticks. It also restores 5 × food Quality energy per tick; an enhanced food item doubles this to 10 × quality.
Without food, InnSlot's actual Tick method restores health but does not restore energy. The class has an EnergyPerTick field, but that field is not used in this implementation.

sections.title: Income and output
paragraphs: Admitting a character below 90% health awards 200 Gold. Assigning food awards round(food SellValue × 0.5) Gold. These payments are credited directly as income.

Finished guests wait for output space, with at most one guest moved to output per update. The class contains a manual-action method that attempts an extra tick on each occupied slot with a 50% chance per guest, but its intrinsically automatic state means the generic craft button is hidden.

articles.title: Barracks, Adventurers Guilds, and mercenaries
articles.summary: Recruit quality, quotas, war gates, and character sale payouts.

sections.title: Recruiting
paragraphs: Barracks produces resources tagged Barracks at a base rate of 0.5 × Speed. Adventurers Guild produces Guild-tagged resources at 0.5 × Speed, but remains blocked until forest war stage 4, checked approximately once per second.

These are resource producers: recruit availability and global quota, per-order payment, worker automation, five-item output buffer, and productivity work as for other resources. Each Recruit Artisan adds 0.1 building Quality and adds 200% of recruit resource value in Gold to each paid order.
Human Quality prestige is added to the quality roll before a new recruit initializes its character data.

sections.title: Mercenary Guild eligibility
paragraphs: Mercenary Guild is intrinsically automatic. It accepts sellable Adventurers with positive SellValue and Quality strictly above 1. Mercenary Conscripts expands eligibility to other HumanItemType characters.
Characters are consumed when sold. The sale pays Gold equal to integer SellValue ÷ 2, plus a Ducat award based on that same halved gold value.

sections.title: Ducat formula
paragraphs: Let D = halved sale value ÷ 5,200. If D is below 1, award one Ducat with probability D. If D is at least 1, award integer(D), discarding the fractional remainder. Gold and Ducats are credited immediately, and the last five transactions are retained for inspection. Human SellValue includes the sell values of currently equipped items, so equipment contributes to both payouts.

related.label: Equipment slots, hands, and armor affinity
War Effort combat, medals, and defense

articles.title: Training Grounds and diminishing returns
articles.summary: Ten training ticks improve humans while consuming energy.

sections.title: Training cycle
paragraphs: Training Grounds accepts HumanItemType. With a Worker, it ticks on a shared timer every 2 ÷ Speed seconds. Each admitted character begins with ten ticks remaining. A manual click independently gives each occupied slot a 50% chance of one additional tick.

Each training tick passes Parent.QualityPerTick × building Quality × repetition factor to AddTraining. QualityPerTick is 0.02 without a training dummy and 0.04 with one. AddTraining first applies trait modifiers, then actually increases item quality by a random amount between half and the full modified parameter; the upper endpoint is excluded.

sections.title: Repeating training
paragraphs: Adventurers always use repetition factor 1. Other humans use 1 on their first training visit, 0.5 on their second, and 0 afterwards. Completing a stay calls ActivityCompleted and increments TrainingCount for Adventurers, or for other humans while TrainingCount is below 3.

Energy lost per tick is 2 × (1 + TrainingCount), halved when the food technology is in use and the character has equipped food. Exhausted characters are removed from the training contents instead of output.

Training Grounds Food makes automatic ticks perform a second tick for a character with food, and equipped food is consumed when the stay completes. Specialization technology checks eligible TrainingGrounds advancements at the halfway tick if the character has not exhausted.

sections.title: Dummy and capacity caveat
paragraphs: Training Grounds Dummy adds an input for nonhuman combatants. A dummy doubles base training gain; trainees that still have positive repetition factor damage it by base damage ÷ 10 each tick. A dead dummy is removed.

The displayed Capacity property is three plus two possible slot technologies. However, GetFreeSlot scans the entire five-element Contents array rather than checking Capacity. This implementation can admit characters into backing slots beyond the displayed capacity; the distinction is relevant when comparing observed behavior with the menu.
Boot Camp has a 10% chance to award one Medal when an exactly quality-1 conscript enters.

articles.title: Arena battles, training, and rewards
articles.summary: The Arena trains combatants and converts completed bouts into currency.

sections.title: Entry and combat
paragraphs: Arena accepts any CombatantItemType in each of two one-item inputs. Eastern war stage 4 must be reached before its update processes entrants. A Worker starts fights automatically; otherwise a bout can be started manually once both slots are filled.

At the start, RewardMultiplier is the product of both combatants' Health01. Each unarmed HumanItemData halves it. Ticks occur every 2 ÷ Speed seconds. Both combatants take simultaneous random damage based on one tenth of the opponent's base damage, with a range from that amount ÷ 1.2 through × 1.2.

Normal bouts stop when a human is below 10% health or a nonhuman is dead. A dead human at the normal stop check is healed by a small random amount. Blood Sport instead continues until a death; if both are dead the code randomly heals one.

sections.title: Training is limited, combat is not
paragraphs: Only the first ten active fight ticks train the slots and cost the normal training energy. After the ten training ticks, combat damage continues until the health/death stop condition is met.

The AddTraining parameter per tick is 0.04, or 0.06 in Blood Sport with two nonhumans, or 0.08 when Blood Sport includes a human. AddTraining applies trait modifiers and actually increases quality by a random amount from half to the full modified parameter. Training is granted only to Adventurers or humans with ArenaCount zero. Energy cost starts at 3 per training tick and scales with 1 + ArenaCount for the eligible humans.

Output eligibility requires a living, nonexhausted human that is an Adventurer or has never completed Arena before. Eligible humans receive ActivityCompleted and an ArenaCount increase. Nonhumans are not output. Nonadventurer humans after their first Arena visit are also not output. Applicable Arena or ArenaWin advancements are then tested.

sections.title: Reward formula
paragraphs: Multiply the starting RewardMultiplier by 1 + 0.1 × Arena Cashier count. For each participant multiply by 1.2 if it is an Adventurer, or 1.1 for other humans. In Blood Sport, multiply by another 1.25 only when the resulting multiplier is above 1.

Currency selection checks sequential thresholds: above 1.5, a 25% Ducat roll; otherwise above 1.25, a 25% Ring roll; otherwise above 1.09, a 25% Crown roll; otherwise Gold. A failed earlier roll can still reach a later eligible currency roll.

Payout is round(10,000 × final multiplier ÷ chosen currency's gold equivalent). Required eligible output slots must have room before completion. Both slots then clear and the Arena waits a four-second cooldown.

articles.title: Shrines, prayer, and Faith
articles.summary: Clerics generate Faith, gain training, and lose increasing energy.

sections.title: Prayer inputs and rewards
paragraphs: Prayer recipes accept any HumanItemType whose Archetype is Cleric. Prayer 1 uses that cleric alone, has a threefold crafting-time multiplier, grants 0.1 training through AddTraining, and produces Faith from a base amount of 27.

Prayer 2 also consumes blessed prayer beads, has a sixfold crafting-time multiplier, grants 0.3 training, and produces Faith from a base amount of 214. Both suppress productivity with BaseProductivity −999.

sections.title: Cleric fatigue and Wisdom
paragraphs: On returning the cleric, OutputCleric(addQL) passes addQL to AddTraining, then costs addQL × 250 × (1 + SpecialCount) energy and increments SpecialCount. AddTraining applies trait modifiers and increases actual item quality by a random amount from half to the full modified training parameter. If the cleric is exhausted it is not returned to the output.

Faith is round(base Faith × craft output quality × max(1, cleric Wisdom ÷ 350)). Wisdom below 350 does not reduce the base reward, while higher Wisdom scales it upward. Faith is credited directly during recipe completion.

sections.title: Other Shrine work
paragraphs: The Shrine spends Faith on blessed prayer beads, indulgence, weapon or equipment blessings, pontiff ring, martyr relic, class transformations, purified technology, upgraded weapons, and cleansed nightmare.

Blessed Arms costs 195 Faith and accepts a weapon that can receive a Blessing; Blessed Equipment costs 145 Faith and accepts nonweapon equipment eligible for a Blessing. Prayer beads cost 84 Faith, indulgence 101, pontiff ring 565, and martyr relic 305 in addition to their listed material inputs.

Purified Tech costs 23 Faith and converts heretic tech with a 10% purified-tech result and 90% return-heretic-tech result. It also suppresses productivity. Cleansed Nightmare costs 1,298 Faith and one reconstructed nightmare.

articles.title: Graveyards and burial services
articles.summary: Burials turn human remains into buried remains and may generate Faith.

sections.title: Burial recipes
paragraphs: Simple Burial consumes one human remains and one coffin. It uses a threefold time multiplier and outputs buried remains at the craft's rolled quality.
Officiated Burial adds a cleric-archetype human, uses a sixfold time multiplier, returns that cleric with 0.15 training and the shared prayer energy cost, and generates Faith from a base of 100.

State Funeral consumes human remains, a gilded coffin, and a cleric plus 15 Crowns. It uses a tenfold time multiplier, adds 0.2 to the buried remains' craft quality, trains the cleric by 0.3, and produces Faith from a base of 290.

sections.title: Special outputs
paragraphs: All three burial recipes set BaseProductivity to −999. Their buried-remains creator only returns an item when the first output buffer currently contains fewer than three items; otherwise that particular result is null.

Because buried-remains output is a custom result rather than a fixed item result, this limit is checked at completion separately from the recipe building's general output-capacity test. Plan a downstream sink for buried remains when using funerals primarily for Faith.

sections.title: Clerics and Faith
paragraphs: Officiating uses Shrine.OutputCleric and Shrine.OutputFaith. Clerics gain escalating SpecialCount energy costs, and exhausted clerics disappear instead of returning. Faith scales with rolled craft quality and max(1, Wisdom ÷ 350), then is rounded and credited directly.

articles.title: Summoning and necromancy
articles.summary: Mana and Faith recipes create combatants or transform existing adventurers.

sections.title: Summoning Circle
paragraphs: Summon Gremlin spends 320 Mana with no item reagents. Summon Hellspawn spends 680 Mana and a gem topaz. Summon Observer spends 390 Mana and an observer eye. These summoning recipes use a crafting-time multiplier of 8.
Faith summons are Cherub for 124 Faith with no item reagents, Valkyrie for 290 Faith plus gold armor, and Arbiter for 475 Faith plus an arcanium greatsword, also at an eightfold time multiplier.

sections.title: Necromancer
paragraphs: Necromancer consumes buried remains to create undead. Shambler costs one buried remains and 460 Mana. Skeletal Archer adds a softwood bow and costs 520 Mana. Skeletal Berserker adds an arcanium ingot and costs 550 Mana. Skeletal Mage adds a gem ruby and costs 990 Mana.
Hulking Monstrosity consumes three buried remains and enchanted cotton thread plus 2,480 Mana. All five undead creation recipes use an eightfold crafting-time multiplier.

sections.title: Class transformations
paragraphs: Demonologist uses a Warlock, blank tome, and gremlin at the Summoning Circle. Necrolyte uses a Warlock, blank tome, and buried remains at the Necromancer. These recipes use a fourfold crafting-time multiplier and BaseProductivity −999.

TransformAdventurer changes the existing human item's type and adds 0.05 training through AddTraining. It preserves the existing item and its character data instead of creating a new independently generated recruit.

articles.title: Inventors, experiments, and Ingenuity
articles.summary: The Inventor converts materials into parts, research currency, and advanced equipment.

sections.title: Tinkering and directed production
paragraphs: Tinker consumes one arcanium ingot, one crystal mana, and one attuned catalyst. With its twofold time multiplier, its default craft time is six seconds. It chooses one Widget, Gizmo, or Doodad with equal configured weights of 0.3333 and gives a base reward of 12 Ingenuity.

Direct part recipes have no item reagents and cost 28 Ingenuity for Widget, 22 for Gizmo, or 26 for Doodad. Their default craft time is 1.5 seconds before building Speed. Completing the Widget recipe triggers Widget Inc.

sections.title: Experiments
paragraphs: Mechanical Experiment consumes a widget and two iron ingots for a base reward of 16 Ingenuity. Alchemical Experiment consumes a gizmo and soothing herbs for 14. Biological Experiment consumes a doodad and stalker eye for 16.
Experiments have no item outputs. Currency rewards follow the normal recipe completion formula: reward base × rolled output quality, rounded. They can therefore operate without an item-output pipe.

sections.title: Advanced material and equipment chain
paragraphs: Inventor combines arcanium ingot and widget into tinkersteel, embroidered cotton and gizmo into witchcloth, and embossed leather and doodad into primal leather. Petrified wood uses resin, attuned catalyst, ancient wood plank, and 4 Ingenuity.

Further recipes spend Ingenuity on winged boots, golem gauntlets, goggles, chainsaw, shield arm, and triune shield. Nightmare Collector consumes nightmare casing, cleansed nightmare, and two decoded writings plus 257 Ingenuity, with a fivefold time multiplier.

articles.title: Incineration and nightmare distillation
articles.summary: Special sinks remove surplus items or advance global nightmare progress.

sections.title: Incinerator
paragraphs: Incinerator accepts every item type except HumanItemType. Each update it consumes its waiting item and records it as LastItem. It produces no output or currency.
Combatant is broader than HumanItemType: nonhuman combatants pass its filter. Human remains are item types rather than living human characters, so eligibility follows the concrete type test.

sections.title: Nightmare Distiller
paragraphs: The building class is NightmareCollector, but its displayed label is Nightmare Distiller. It accepts the nightmare_collector item and has no craft button.

While global NightmareProgress is below 1, it consumes one collector and adds 1 ÷ floor(square root of NightmareCount) to that global progress. Values above 0.985 but still below 1 are snapped to 1. It does not consume collectors once progress is already at least 1.

The node reads and writes the player's shared progress rather than keeping a separate pool per building. Its formula has no explicit zero-count guard in this class, so the progression system's current NightmareCount is part of interpreting the requirement.

articles.title: Map navigation and dragging
articles.summary: Camera scales, click-to-move, drag-to-move, snapping, and cancellation.

sections.title: Camera
paragraphs: WASD moves the world or technology camera. Movement speed scales with 5−zoomLevel. Zoom levels 0–4 use scales 0.25, 0.5, 1, 2, and 4; maximum level is 3 on screens no taller than 1400 unless UI scale exceeds 1, otherwise 4. Zoom adjusts around the mouse. Bounds surround placed machines with about 1000 world units of margin; technology bounds surround visible tech nodes.

sections.title: Click or drag
paragraphs: DragDropManager supports holding the left mouse button and releasing to drop, or clicking once to pick up and again to drop. New drags are blocked during deconstruction and the initial tutorial blackout. Text fields delay normal player shortcuts while focused.

sections.title: Move a machine
paragraphs: Click or drag its title label. Ctrl bypasses grid snapping. Dropping onto another machine restores its prior position. Cancel restores its old position unless it has already been transferred to another workflow. Moving a single machine to another workflow disconnects all of its pipes.

FlowCollider separates dragged machines into another layer; collision tests reject machine overlaps, while decorations are allowed behind machines. Prefab lookup uses the machine ElementType to select its UI, decorative background, and category title border.

articles.title: Pipes, waypoints, and port inspection
articles.summary: Connect, reroute, disconnect, and inspect the items inside production lines.

sections.title: Connections
paragraphs: Left click or drag a port to begin a connection; finish at a port of the opposite direction. Existing connections on either endpoint are disconnected before the new link is made. Starting from an already connected input reroutes from that pipe’s output. Starting from a connected output clears its waypoints first. Right click a connected port to disconnect it.

sections.title: Waypoints
paragraphs: While routing a pipe, Ctrl-click empty space to add a waypoint and continue drawing. Waypoints can be clicked/dragged, snapped to an offset grid, or positioned freely with Ctrl. Right click a waypoint removes it. Canceling a waypoint move restores its old coordinate. Pipe rendering and collider geometry follow all waypoints.

sections.title: Status colors
paragraphs: A transferred item briefly flashes the pipe white; rejected items set it dark red; timeout flashes dark orange. Port artwork also switches to an error sprite when its connected pipe rejected an item. These are feedback signals from the pipe model.

sections.title: Inspect buffers
paragraphs: Hover a port for its item icon preview and buffered count; when empty it can cycle among previewable accepted item types. Hold Shift while hovering for the full item tooltip. Shift-right-click a human item opens character details. Output ports normally buffer one item; FlowInput adds an item only when CanBuffer permits it.

articles.title: Machine stacks, mirrored ports, and upgrade slots
articles.summary: Additional mouse gestures and how upgrade replacement charges and refunds work.

sections.title: Stack and mirror
paragraphs: After element_stacking, Ctrl-left-click a stackable machine to add one copy, up to stack size 5. The game charges GetSingleCopyCost, updates upgrade effects and label, and shows the stack as layered backgrounds. It does not stack while deconstructing or when the pointer is on a Button or port. Alt-left-click flips Mirrored and rebuilds port positions and pipe lines.

sections.title: Picker
paragraphs: Middle click after unlock_picker opens a configured purchase copy if affordable. Pointer travel exceeding 50 world units suppresses accidental clicks after panning.

sections.title: Upgrade slots
paragraphs: Click a slot to see Remove plus available researched upgrades. Hover an option to see its effect at the relevant nth duplicate, its purchase cost, and any old-upgrade refund. Selecting a different type charges the new price and refunds the old upgrade; selecting Remove only refunds. Selecting the same upgrade type opens/closes the chooser without buying a second copy.

With easy_node_upgrade, Ctrl-clicking a slot asks the machine for its automatic recommended upgrade and attempts to buy that. Progress bars show current crafting and productivity; the full-output warning appears after completed progress remains blocked for more than 0.1 seconds.

articles.title: Decorations, labels, colors, and stickers
articles.summary: Buying and editing layout decorations and their exact base prices.

sections.title: Editing containers and labels
paragraphs: Decoration research exposes containers; deco_label and deco_sticker expose their additional rows. The options popup edits style index, lock state, anchor/parent state, and label text. Style choices select one of the prefab’s background-color sprites; this code does not expose an arbitrary RGB color picker. Labels resize to preferred text width+96 and height+32. Enter ends label editing and closes the popup.

sections.title: Stickers
paragraphs: A sticker selects an icon from item, technology, and currency icon names. Search uses a case-insensitive name substring. Size is a slider integer multiplied by 64, keeping a square footprint. Selecting an icon changes it immediately; double clicking an icon also saves/closes. Stickers use alpha hit-testing so transparent pixels are not the full clickable rectangle.

sections.title: Persistence and copy
paragraphs: FlowDeco saves position, size, style, optional sticker data, label, lock and parent flags. IconSticker saves IconName and uses the standard sticker cost. CreateCopy copies style/size/label/parent/sticker, but does not copy Locked in this implementation. Sticker factories reconstruct the subtype from its saved Type.

related.label: Workflow tabs, names, icons, and ordering
Data records, serialization, and implementation limits

articles.title: Container anchors, resizing, and group movement
articles.summary: How decorated areas collect machines, labels, and pipe waypoints.

sections.title: Anchored parts
paragraphs: An IsParent decoration gathers overlapping machines, decorations, and pipe waypoints. It recursively follows parent decorations, deduplicates machines/decorations, and normally excludes other containers unless requested. Turning Anchor off makes the decoration move alone. Labels can be parents too.

sections.title: Move and resize
paragraphs: Use the move handle to pick up a parent and its anchored parts. Ctrl bypasses the layout grid. On drop, any overlapping anchored machine causes the complete group to revert. Cancel also reverts unless the group has crossed to another workflow. Resize from a corner; minimum width and height are 64. Cancel restores old position and size.

sections.title: Move between workflows
paragraphs: A group transfer retains pipes with both endpoints in the moved machine set and transfers their waypoints; crossing-boundary connections are disconnected. Decorations and anchored pipe nodes move with it. The temporary parent used by area-move is destroyed afterward.

sections.title: Lock and clone
paragraphs: Lock hides normal move/edit/resize controls and exposes an unlock control. At far zoom levels the edit button is hidden and move handles scale up. Middle click copies an affordable decorated group after container_clone. Clicking a parent label can locate the overlapping container for that clone action.

articles.title: Deconstruction and refunds
articles.summary: Remove machines, decoration groups, pipes, and waypoints.

sections.title: Pointer target determines the action
paragraphs: In deconstruct mode, releasing the left button removes the target. A connected port takes precedence over its machine and disconnects its pipe. A pipe waypoint removes only that waypoint. A machine removes that machine; a decoration removes the decoration. The displayed refund refreshes roughly every 0.1 seconds.

sections.title: Shift removes anchored contents
paragraphs: Holding Shift while deconstructing a parent decoration also removes its anchored machines and decorations. The decoration refund path adds machine refunds when anchored contents are included. Without Shift the contents remain. Decorations refund half their own purchase cost. Refunds are not income for earned-Gold statistics.

sections.title: Preview before dropping
paragraphs: The overlay shows the available refund collection. It does not refund a whole machine merely for disconnecting a port. Moving groups and individual machine drags have separate collision/cancel behavior; they are not purchases unless a copy blueprint is used.

articles.title: Build menu and recipe selection
articles.summary: Categories, search, selected recipes, ingredient previews, and changing machine configuration.

sections.title: Build categories and search
paragraphs: The build menu lists buildable machine types under category tabs. Empty categories are gray and cannot be selected. Search hides the tabs and matches all typed words, case-insensitively, against translated label or description. Blank search produces no result list in this implementation.

sections.title: Recipe selection
paragraphs: The current recipe is shown first above a spacer, followed by the other recipes available to that machine. Search matches every nonempty word against recipe name or description. Changing machine type resets the search state. Each recipe row shows reagent icons/counts and direct currency crafting costs; hovering shows equipment slot, description and detailed recipe results.

sections.title: Changing a recipe
paragraphs: Selection clears and rebuilds the machine’s IO and refreshes its label/icon. The adapter attempts to reconnect old pipes by matching port indices that still exist. Input-side reconnections retain their old waypoints; output-side reconstruction does not explicitly copy them. Do not assume changing recipes preserves the meaning of each indexed ingredient connection.

sections.title: Tutorial behavior
paragraphs: Recipe selection is blocked during the initial blackout. New machine and recipe adapters often open a configuration popup one frame after placement. Several ReopenBuyMenu properties are recorded but their selection callbacks only discard the value, so they are not a reliable promise that every configuration returns to the build menu.

articles.title: The in-game item encyclopedia
articles.summary: Find an item’s sources, recipes, and configured machine shortcuts.

sections.title: Unlock-aware item list
paragraphs: ItemMenu builds rows from ItemType.Unlocked. Clicking expands a row; expanding another collapses the previous row. Search requires all words in the translated item name, case-insensitively. It searches names rather than every recipe description.

sections.title: Sources and uses
paragraphs: An expanded row lists item description, crafting recipes producing it, resource suppliers, Forest, source quests/dungeons, training, or Arena where applicable. A second list shows recipes that consume it. Empty categories show a no-source/no-recipe message. Source lists are populated lazily when first expanded.

sections.title: Build directly from a source
paragraphs: Click or drag an available source entry to buy a machine preconfigured for that recipe/resource/quest/dungeon. Affordability is checked before the purchase ghost opens. Locked entries display their research requirement if available, otherwise a generic locked label. An item appearing in the encyclopedia does not grant every recipe that uses it.

sections.title: Implementation detail affecting expectations
paragraphs: ItemMenu keeps built rows and toggles their visibility during search. Blank active search returns early, rather than explicitly restoring every row; turning search off calls ShowAll. Recipe availability and dungeon unlock sets independently control whether a source can be placed.

articles.title: Resource quotas and supplier configuration
articles.summary: Read resource demand and buy capacity without confusing it with item inventory.

sections.title: Quota panel
paragraphs: ResourcesMenu lists available resources except Farm resources and AdventureSupplies. Each row refreshes available capacity and demand, highlights demand red above supply, and offers the next quota increase at GamePlayer.GetResourceUpgrade’s current cost. Buying spends that collection and adds the quota with isUpgrade=true.

sections.title: Supplier choice
paragraphs: The selector shows the machine’s current resource first, then other resources available for its supply tag. Resource demand is live; available capacity is shown explicitly below 5000. Selection clears/rebuilds that resource machine’s IO and refreshes its label/icon.

sections.title: Costs and output warnings
paragraphs: Hover a resource for its description and per-resource collection cost where applicable. The world adapter shows queue count only above 1, hides it when Output Full is displayed, and marks blocked output when OutputPerSecond is zero. Capacity and demand are rate/quota information, not a count of loose items waiting in storage.

sections.title: Shortcut
paragraphs: The resource-window shortcut is visible only after unlock_supply_window and is omitted for Farm and AdventureSupplies.

articles.title: Forest crew and harvest controls
articles.summary: Assign workers, hire more crew, compare utilization, and select harvest outputs.

sections.title: Hiring and assigning
paragraphs: Hire Crew buys one unassigned worker at NextWorkerCost. A role’s + button assigns one unassigned worker; Ctrl assigns all unassigned workers. When none remain, + instead attempts to buy and assign one. The − button removes one worker; Ctrl removes the full role allocation. Subtract is disabled at zero.

sections.title: Utilization and blocking
paragraphs: Role tabs show utilization every 0.2 seconds and color it red above 100%. The menu and resource selector show the global blocked state. Animated work scenes are hidden when blocked or when that role has no workers. Tooltips list each role’s harvest items and WorkersPerItem.

sections.title: Choosing a Forest output
paragraphs: The selector groups resources by worker role and remembers the last category. It shows the currently selected resource first if it belongs to that category. Rows show description and harvest costs. Selecting another resource rebuilds the Forest machine’s IO. Its world tooltip includes quality, maximum output, harvest cost and role utilization.

articles.title: Farm plots and planting controls
articles.summary: Paint crops/animals, clear plots, copy a plot choice, and expand the field.

sections.title: Paint and clear
paragraphs: Click or drag a resource from the Farm list to pick up its ghost. Dropping on a plot sets that resource and keeps the ghost active for repeated planting. Dropping elsewhere cancels. Right click a plot with no planting ghost clears it; middle click a populated plot picks its resource for reuse. Closing Farm cancels the drag.

sections.title: Expansion
paragraphs: The panel creates each plot at 58-pixel spacing. A right-edge expansion adds a column while Width<6; bottom expansion adds a row. Buying uses GetPlotCost(numberOfNewPlots), enlarges field size, and rebuilds the panel. Width is capped in this interface by hiding column extensions at six; no equivalent height cap is visible in FarmMenu.

sections.title: Read yield and demand
paragraphs: Resource tooltips show description and PlotYield. The list compares demand/available quota, displays nonzero utilization as a percentage, and turns it red above 100%. Plot background details are deterministic from plot coordinates and a FarmMenuPlot seed; they are decorative, not differing soil statistics.

articles.title: Filters, Appraisers, and Accountants
articles.summary: Choose exact item filters, stat comparisons, and balance-based gates.

sections.title: Filter
paragraphs: Filter’s selector lists unlocked item types. Search matches all words against translated item names. Selecting an item changes its icon and closes the popup. Filter sends exact matching ItemType to output index 0 and other items to index 1. A full chosen output stalls the item instead of using the other output.

sections.title: Appraiser
paragraphs: Choose a stat, comparison operator, and integer amount. Operators are ==, !=, <, <=, >, and >=. Current Health, Current Energy, Quality, and Training are marked as percentages; other stats use their numeric units. No selected stat passes every item. True goes to output 0, false to output 1; routing waits when the selected output is full.

sections.title: Accountant
paragraphs: Choose a currency, operator and whole-number threshold to open/close a single output. It compares the kingdom balance, not the passing item value. No currency selected passes everything. Gold comparison uses balance/10000, i.e. whole displayed gold coins, whereas other currencies use whole currency units.

sections.title: Applying settings
paragraphs: Enter or numpad Enter submits Appraiser/Accountant edits. Empty amount text becomes zero. Applying updates model, icon and displayed threshold and closes the popup. Appraiser current-health/current-energy values are rounded percentages of combatant maximums.

articles.title: Armory and Portal configuration
articles.summary: Input/output modes, eight colors, numbered subchannels, and shared inventories.

sections.title: Armory
paragraphs: The popup has eight color channels. Channel selectors are hidden unless the machine’s ChannelTech is owned. Choose the Input row to store items, or an available compatible item type to output it. Available output types are sorted by item ordinal; rows show stored count and peek-item tooltips.

sections.title: Safe mode switching behavior
paragraphs: Switching from output to input clears outputs; switching from input to output clears inputs. Changing an output type returns the currently connected pipe’s input/output buffers to the Armory channel and clears those buffers before reconfiguring the output. Changing channels refreshes colors and item choices.

sections.title: Portal
paragraphs: The Portal popup always builds eight color choices and eight numbered index choices. Numbered indices are shown after portal_unlock_channels; the labels are 1–8 while storage uses indices 0–7. Choose Input or Output to set its direction. Changing an output Portal’s color or index first clears its output. Index contents refresh about every 0.2 seconds.

sections.title: Find linked stores
paragraphs: World Armory and Portal adapters show channel colors and live item/count information. Their cycle action finds the next related machine and calls ShowElement, allowing navigation to another linked storage endpoint. Empty stores have no fabricated item tooltip.

articles.title: Quest Board panel controls
articles.summary: Expand and accept quests, preview challenges, and read repeat rewards and party status.

sections.title: Choose or inspect
paragraphs: The Quest popup lists unlocked quests. The board’s current quest is marked, expanded, and moved to the top. Clicking a different collapsed row expands its description/challenges/rewards; the Accept button actually assigns it, updates the board IO, and closes the popup. Merely expanding does not accept.

sections.title: Live details
paragraphs: Difficulty, challenge icons and party contents are shown. Progress is refreshed roughly once per second; no tick progress hides the progress bar. Reward rows are rebuilt when completed count changes using GetRewards(completedCount), so first-clear and repeat rewards can differ. Completed-count text distinguishes never completed from repeated clears.

sections.title: Tooltips and party
paragraphs: Hover challenge icons for full challenge content; challenge rows show their description. Reward tooltips appear only if the reward supplies a TooltipTitle. Right-clicking a human in the party opens details and can return to this popup on closing. QuestBoardPopup refuses normal Cancel while a tooltip is active.

sections.title: World presentation
paragraphs: The world board selects a quest-specific background and character positions where supplied, otherwise its default art/layout. Adding adventurers fills visible slots; quest completion clears their sprites. These UI placements are not extra party members or combat bonuses.

articles.title: Dungeon selection and expedition display
articles.summary: Inspect stages, boss health, wipe counts, parties, and retreat controls.

sections.title: Select a dungeon
paragraphs: The selection popup lists DungeonType.Unlocked, not every dungeon defined in code. Rows show icon, description and TotalSupplyCost, which includes nightmare scaling where applicable. Left click assigns it to the world machine; Inspect opens the detailed dungeon panel instead.

sections.title: Dungeon tabs and stage nodes
paragraphs: Detailed panels create tabs for unlocked dungeons, split after three tabs. Clicking a progress node selects a visible stage for inspection; it does not move the expedition to that stage. Each stage displays its difficulty, challenges, rewards, completion count and wipe count. A cleared-stage label appears when current stage is later.

sections.title: Active versus inspected stage
paragraphs: The party is displayed on the active stage, sorted by DistanceRank. Other inspected stages hide party sprites. Active trash stages show walking and scrolling backgrounds; active bosses show fighting and boss-health progress; a finished stage is idle. The progress tracker follows the current expedition, even when another stage is being inspected.

sections.title: Retreat and status
paragraphs: Retreat is offered while the party has members and calls DungeonProgress.DoRetreat. Empty parties show Waiting to Start. StatusText, stage counters and party indicators update frequently. Companion trait art can appear beside an adventurer without creating another combatant entry. Challenge badges indicate success and fade; boss hit/death colors are visual feedback.

sections.title: Presentation data
paragraphs: WorldDungeonSprite pairs IDs with machine backgrounds; DungeonScrollingBackground pairs IDs with a default and optional per-stage background. Scrolling uses tiled images and only runs during an active trash fight. These structures contain art selections rather than hidden rewards.

articles.title: War selection and status panels
articles.summary: Choose a campaign, read progress trends, inspect stage rewards, and examine soldiers.

sections.title: Campaign choice
paragraphs: The machine popup lists wars already present in GamePlayer.Wars. Select assigns the machine’s WarType; Inspect opens the campaign panel. Rows refresh current stage and stage progress. A completed North campaign has its own status wording. The world machine opens its selector if no campaign is set, otherwise its details.

sections.title: Status colors
paragraphs: The war panel creates tabs for available wars, stage nodes and a progress strip. Blocked progression is red with ProgressBlockedReason. Tracker above 2 is green, below 2 red, and exactly 2 neutral blue. After the final stage, a complete status replaces the current-stage line.

sections.title: Stage rewards
paragraphs: Hover a stage node for description and reward text. Secured stages show RewardComplete; others show the prospective RewardDescription. Stage icons become colored when HasWarStage reports them secured. Terrain and enemy artwork are selected from campaign data.

sections.title: Soldiers
paragraphs: The soldier panel shows at most its MaxCount (default 10), plus an overflow count; this is a display limit rather than an army cap. Sprites show weapon and health. Tooltips warn humans lacking weapons and combatants lacking armor. Right click a human for details and return to the war panel on closing. Health gains flash green, losses pale red; death/exhaustion fades the portrait.

articles.title: Character, training, recovery, and Arena displays
articles.summary: Inspect equipped humans and interpret training slots, outfitting and fight-state indicators.

sections.title: Human details
paragraphs: Character details show the seeded personal name, displayed level (internal Level+1), class/item name, quality, health, energy, combat power, four main stats, equipment, traits and advancement options. Empty equipment slots show a gray slot label/icon and no item tooltip; filled slots show their full item. Armor tooltip calculates damage reduction rather than merely repeating the armor number.

sections.title: Advancement visibility
paragraphs: The panel marks available advancement options and shows a locked state until TrainingGrounds.SpecUnlock. Available markers reflect each advancement’s predicate; these small UI components provide descriptions/availability rather than a manual purchase button. Traits and advancement lists rebuild when their source list changes.

sections.title: Training and Inn slots
paragraphs: Training slot portraits show progress, current human, and a transformation animation when its icon changes. Inn reuses this widget for five slots, including any current food icon. Right click a human in a slot opens details. Empty slots disable item tooltips; spawn/leave/evolve animations are presentation.

sections.title: Outfitter
paragraphs: Manual outfitting button queues an action once; automated mode shows a progress bar instead. Inspect opens the current or last human. After outfitter_timeout, the timeout popup sets seconds in half-second steps (slider/2); zero is labeled None. Releasing the slider commits/closes the popup.

sections.title: Arena
paragraphs: Arena displays two combatants, their health and fighting/idle animations. War blocking replaces both slots with blocked artwork. Manual fight button appears only when manual crafting is possible and automation is off. Output Full indicates blocked production. Right click a human slot to inspect it.

sections.title: Power and equipment terminology
paragraphs: Weapon slot wording distinguishes two-handed, ambidextrous one-handed, and fixed-slot weapons. Armor/slot/stat extension methods supply localized names. Combatant tooltips show live health, quality above baseline, armor, combat power and description.

articles.title: Production status, routing buttons, and recent results
articles.summary: Read sales, refinery results, buffers, and the small controls built into machines.

sections.title: Sales and disenchanting
paragraphs: Shop shows collected Gold capped by MaxGold and a recent-sales tooltip with item quality and received value. Restaurant and Luxury Shop show Gold plus Crowns; Mercenary Guild shows Gold plus Ducats. Empty histories say no recent sales. Quality above baseline is green and below baseline red.
Disenchanter shows collected Mana and recent items with failure explanations: quality below 1.04, no enhancement, or both. The tooltip lists each item’s ManaValue.

sections.title: Refiner and Inspector
paragraphs: Refiner tooltip reports the last item, original/new quality, destruction when new quality is zero, and Mana spent. With refiner_mana, its control toggles Mana use. Inspector blinks when its last item changes, refreshes full item details, and opens human details from live item or the last item. Incinerator shows a fading red-tinted icon when it consumes a new last item.

sections.title: Collector, Distributor, Manifold
paragraphs: Their small plus control adds ports until four, then becomes a collapse control. Collector and Manifold add inputs; Distributor adds outputs. Despite its UI method name AddOutputSlot, Manifold’s adapter calls AddInputSlot. Hovering shows the last passing item when one exists.

sections.title: Track switch
paragraphs: Left click toggles SwitchPosition. Hover changes switch artwork; a missing secondary connection can gray its image. The switch’s routes and production model remain separate from the tooltip/animation adapter.

sections.title: Requisition Office
paragraphs: Its world display shows accumulated Requisition. Selecting a contract changes the shared index used by that office. Reroll costs currency and replaces that index across the kingdom; every placed office using the index updates its input. Reroll control is hidden before requisition_office_reroll. Conversion text is contract.BaseValue divided by Requisition reference value.

articles.title: Workflow tabs, names, icons, and ordering
articles.summary: Switch diagrams, buy additional diagrams, rename them, and swap their positions.

sections.title: Switch and reorder
paragraphs: Left click another workflow tab to switch. Ctrl-left-click another tab swaps its position with the currently active workflow, updating indices and selection. Right click opens its name/icon options. First ten workflows show the corresponding configurable numeric hotkey when its label fits.

sections.title: Scroll and overflow
paragraphs: Mouse wheel over the workflow bar cycles the current diagram with wraparound. Left/right overflow buttons move the visible tab window. Available width depends on screen width and UI scale and caps at ten buttons, including the Add button. Hover slides the tab bar into view; an open options popup postpones that motion.

sections.title: Names and icons
paragraphs: Type a label in options; PopupClosed writes it to the workflow. Icon selection applies immediately and refreshes the bar. Search matches icon names case-insensitively, using icons from items, nondeveloper technologies and currencies. Enter saves/closes; double click an icon selects it and saves.

sections.title: Buy a workflow
paragraphs: The Add button shows GetExtraWorkflowCost in its tooltip. Buying spends it, appends a new FlowDiagram, refreshes tabs, and immediately switches to the new one. All workflows still simulate through GamePlayer.Update when not selected.

related.label: Data records, serialization, and implementation limits

articles.title: Research tree and list interface
articles.summary: Navigate branches, locate technologies, and distinguish visible clues from purchasable nodes.

sections.title: Tree navigation
paragraphs: Opening research shows the global tree; selecting an owned root opens its child branch. Clicking the same root again returns global. The War branch also displays War-type nodes and the Dungeon branch Dungeon-type nodes. Hidden technologies are filtered out. Camera position and zoom are saved on the player.

sections.title: Availability cues
paragraphs: Available nodes show price, glow and purchase behavior. Locked nodes use unknown/gray states; a node’s identity may appear when an adjacent prerequisite is available or purchased. Custom unmet requirements are appended in red. Owned roots show counts of currently available children and a new-tech indicator based on the last seen count.

sections.title: Research list
paragraphs: global_tech_upgrade exposes the list button. The list groups available roots, available children, locked nodes, and purchased nodes. Left click buys an available row after affordability check; right click an unlocked row focuses that node in its branch. The inspected implementation appends purchased nodes through two loops, so duplicate purchased rows can appear.

sections.title: Exit behavior and dormant code
paragraphs: Escape closes list first, then a branch, then research. Cancel can return from a branch if the pointer was not dragged far; right-clicking a list row is reserved for locate. UIElementTechNode contains child-purchase helper code, but _childPurchaseActive always returns false in this inspected build, so that shortcut is dormant.

related.label: Data records, serialization, and implementation limits

articles.title: Currency HUD and coin denominations
articles.summary: Interpret raw Gold units, copper/silver/gold icons, affordability, and exchange clicks.

sections.title: One stored Gold unit is the smallest coin unit
paragraphs: Currency.Gold is stored as an integer, but the UI splits it into denominations: copper=amount%100, silver=(amount/100)%100, gold=amount/10000. Thus 100 raw Gold units display as 1 silver and 10,000 as 1 gold. Source-derived numeric costs in raw collections must be converted before labeling them displayed gold coins.

sections.title: Compact HUD
paragraphs: The currency pane refreshes about every 0.2 seconds. With fewer than four currency kinds it forces copper visible; below six it retains silver. More populated HUDs can hide small denominations to fit. Hovering while a tooltip is active postpones rebuilding the currency rows. Values in tooltips also use coin denominations and can omit copper when gold is present.

sections.title: Cost and value displays
paragraphs: CurrencyDisplay can mark insufficient balances with a configured color and show No Cost for an empty collection. CurrencyDisplayLite presents machine income with a specialist currency beside coins. TooltipCost rebuilds its layout; TooltipValue presents a compact multi-currency value line.

sections.title: Exchange gesture
paragraphs: After currency_exchange, left click a tradeable non-Gold currency cell to buy, right click to sell. Mana, Ingenuity and Faith display an exchange-disabled message. Hover shows the currency description. This shortcut applies to currency cells carrying their tooltip/component, not arbitrary artwork shaped like coins.

articles.title: Tooltips, warnings, notifications, and tutorial cues
articles.summary: How contextual details, text input, progress bars, and alert messages behave.

sections.title: Tooltips
paragraphs: TooltipSource obtains title, body and custom content from its configured object or parent interfaces. Hover shows a tooltip only when the component is enabled and drag/drop is not busy. Exiting hides it or forwards to the newly hovered tooltip source. Tooltips follow the mouse, flip horizontally/vertically near screen edges and include text, item rows, prices, values, separators and progress bars.

sections.title: Live content and layout
paragraphs: TinyProgressBar refreshes its callbacks every 0.5 seconds. ItemCountCell provides an item tooltip only for actual item entries; arbitrary icon/text cells disable it. TextContainer sizes itself to preferred text plus padding. FontFilteringSwitch selects point-font rendering when effective size rounds to 16, otherwise the filtered font; changes propagate separately to world and screen-space text.

sections.title: Warnings and status
paragraphs: A disabled craft button reports Output Full when progress≥1, otherwise No Ingredients. Status notifications last five simulated seconds unless persistent, slide/fade in and fade out, and can invoke a click action. Persistent notifications expose a close control. General alerts support Okay or Yes/No with supplied callbacks and resize around localized message text.

sections.title: Input helpers
paragraphs: Focused text fields repeatedly delay player input. HoverAction and RightClickAction invoke configured UI events, HoverHighlight toggles artwork, and DepressButton shifts button children down two pixels while pressed. UIBlocksZoom prevents world zoom while hovering registered menus/popups. These are presentation/input wrappers rather than extra game systems.

sections.title: Tutorial sequence
paragraphs: Initial blackout prevents normal dragging and recipe selection. Dismissing it re-enables controls/UI and fades the overlay. Tutorial arrows direct construction, Mine upgrade slots, output-to-Forge connection, research and the Shop unlock. Opening the relevant crew/resource/build panel clears its cue. FinishTutorial disables the tutorial component; arrow blinking/motion is visual guidance.

articles.title: Menus, save selection, music, and visual feedback
articles.summary: Menu rows, rebinding restrictions, audio timing, and cosmetic animation behavior.

sections.title: Save and Load rows
paragraphs: Rows are sorted newest-first and display filename plus dd/MM/yyyy HH:mm:ss filesystem time. One click selects/highlights; double click executes the current save/load action. Save selection copies the name into the editable field; blank names do nothing; Enter saves and resumes. Load executes only after a selected file exists and routes to main-menu or in-game loading.

sections.title: Key rebinding restrictions
paragraphs: The listening row accepts keyboard controls, excluding mouse, AnyKey and standalone Shift/Ctrl/Alt variants. Escape cancels listening. Only one row listens at a time; a newly selected row cancels other listeners. Apply/Cancel behavior is handled by KeyBindingsUI.

sections.title: Music
paragraphs: Music volume defaults to 0.35 and sound volume to 1 in PlayerPrefs. MusicLibrary defines tracks per machine/scene. The manager shuffles its normal playlist, changes after about 300 simulated seconds, and supports fades and quiet gaps. Hovering machines queues their theme only after elapsed-time thresholds; it does not immediately restart every hovered song. Victory and prestige use dedicated tracks.

sections.title: Sound and cosmetic animation
paragraphs: UISounds caches audio sources, varies pitch slightly and suppresses the same clip for 0.1 unscaled seconds to limit repeated clicks. Releasing the sound slider previews a page sound. Floating messages rise and fade; falling menu item icons and the bobbing logo are cosmetic. Prestige background wobble and victory music contain no additional progression rules.

sections.title: Boot and new-game transition
paragraphs: Bootstrap initializes translation before scene load, keeps Bootstrap roots alive, applies settings and initializes Steam stats if Steam is available. New Game fades a transition, creates the player, sets zoom from screen height, loads Game, displays tutorial content, hides ordinary UI and disables controls until tutorial dismissal.

articles.title: Data records, serialization, and implementation limits
articles.summary: Support code that stores game state and presents names, stats, rewards, and assets.

sections.title: Items and stats
paragraphs: ItemData links to its InventoryItem and serializes Type plus subtype fields; reconstruction uses the saved type string then loads subtype data. CraftingInput stores lists of consumed inputs per reagent slot and serializes them as arrays. StatSet uses an enum-indexed integer array, yields only nonzero values, and saves nonzero entries by stat name. GameConstants derives stat/enhancement/equipment counts from their enums.

sections.title: Resource and enhancement metadata
paragraphs: ResourceItemType holds quota defaults (1 amount, 1.2 cost multiplier, base cost 1950 raw Gold units), optional harvest costs and a resource tag. Positive available quota can make it unlocked independently of normal recipe unlocks. Forest/Farm types defer visibility to their settings. ItemEnhancement finds its default recipe, derives its base value from recipe result count, scales described stats by quality, and serializes itself as its identifier.

sections.title: Quest, dungeon and war records
paragraphs: QuestMetadata saves a quest ID and completed count. DungeonMetadata saves per-stage completed and wipe arrays and loads older records with a missing wipe array. QuestReward defines both quest and dungeon reward entry points; CustomReward invokes the configured action in either context. WarStage stores descriptions/rewards, combat requirements and completion callback; WarType registers four campaigns and exposes a two-second TickDelay.

sections.title: Names and localization records
paragraphs: AdventurerName combines given/family names and culture fields. AdventurerIdentity optionally adds a title after a comma, but the shown human-details name uses HumanNameGenerator directly. CultureProfile, SurnamePattern and WeightedOption contain the syllable pools, patterns and positive weights explained in Character names. Armor, equipment slot, stat, category and worker extension methods supply @translation keys.

sections.title: Registers, helpers and assets
paragraphs: Register stores named boolean flags, integer counters and string data on the player, with defaults for missing keys and JSON objects for each collection. ClassExtensions provides serialization helpers, enum-key conversion, snake_case identifiers, translated TMP text, integer-vector conversion and recursive UI cleanup/lookups. Materials supplies normal and grayscale materials. SpriteLibrary loads Icons, Icons2, Icons3 and AnimationFrames resource sheets and builds icon choices from items, nondeveloper research and currencies.

sections.title: Version and completeness caveats
paragraphs: GameVersion parses a trailing major.minor.patch and compares components for old-save patches. The inspected C# defines behavior and references serialized scenes/prefabs, fonts, sprites, audio and localized text; it cannot by itself prove every inspector-assigned event, slider bound, visual asset or Steam backend rule. This article documents support code without treating record fields or dormant helper methods as secret playable systems.

related.label: Workflow tabs, names, icons, and ordering

articles.title: Starting a kingdom
articles.summary: The exact new-game state and first production chain.

sections.title: Starting state
paragraphs: A new player receives mine and forge technologies, the iron_ingot recipe, and mine_iron_ore through the mine callback. Iron-ore resource capacity starts at 1. The only placed machine is a Forge configured for iron ingots at world position (-128,64), with five iron-ore items buffered in its first input. There is one workflow and no initial currency grant in CreateNewPlayer.

Shop is a free technology after Forge, but is not explicitly pre-purchased by CreateNewPlayer. Blacksmith grants iron_armor; Supply Depot additionally requires Mine automation and grants the wood-plank supply technology. Technology grants do not place machines.

sections.title: New Game and Continue
paragraphs: The main menu clears the in-memory player. New Game calls Bootstrap.InitNewGame; Continue loads the newest save by filesystem last-write time. GameManager tries the latest save if no in-memory player exists and creates a new player only if no latest save exists. A corrupt newest save can raise a load error; LoadLatestSave does not search older files automatically.

sections.title: Every workflow runs
paragraphs: WorldFlowManager starts and updates GamePlayer with Unity Time.deltaTime. Player resource quota recalculates on roughly 0.1-second ticks, war progress on roughly 2-second ticks, and GameTime counts simulated seconds. Every workflow is updated, including workflows not currently selected.

articles.title: Technology requirements and unlocking
articles.summary: Parents, prerequisite lists, special gates, hidden content, and purchases.

sections.title: Requirements combine
paragraphs: A node is locked when Root is unpurchased, Previous is unpurchased, any AdditionalRequirements entry is unpurchased, or CustomRequirement returns false. Root organizes the branch and also gates it; Previous expresses another purchase prerequisite. Available means unpurchased, unlocked, and not Hidden for this player.

HasWarStage(type,stage) checks current war stage index ≥ stage. Since completed stages advance the index, a requirement stated as stage 1 means finishing the first stage, not merely having the war unlocked.

sections.title: Branch tier versus cost tier
paragraphs: The eleven tier articles group declarations by their T1–T11 source-class prefix. An early branch can contain late-game recipes with higher explicit cost tiers. An unspecified cost tier inherits from Previous, otherwise Root. A missing Root inherits Previous.Root when available. Default currency is set from the resulting cost tier.

Tier tables list every explicit new TechNode declaration. Shared automation helpers add further nodes, explained in Automation technology. Declared cost overrides take precedence over defaults. Resolved entity data and the in-game tooltip give the final price.

sections.title: Purchases and grants
paragraphs: A left click on an available node spends its full currency collection, marks it unlocked, invokes OnUnlock, updates the tree, and refreshes the tooltip. Free technologies can still need a click unless an unlock callback grants them. AddTech rejects DevMode nodes.

sections.title: Hidden and developer content
paragraphs: dev_item_spawner is DevMode. turtle_statue is always hidden. Several store-channel technologies are also always hidden, and graveyard_productivity is hidden after its default upgrade is created. Tier tables mark explicit hidden declarations. The all-tech achievement excludes hidden and developer nodes. Code presence alone does not prove normal availability.

related.label: Technology tier 11: Faith, undead, and endgame
Quest challenges, rewards, and permanent discounts

articles.title: Automation and shared machine upgrades
articles.summary: Worker, extra slots, quality, and productivity research.

sections.title: Default family
paragraphs: AddDefaultUpgrades creates Worker, second slot, productivity, quality, and third slot technologies. Some branches use custom subsets or replace prices afterward. These researches allow upgrades or slots; they do not purchase and install the actual worker or upgrade on every machine.

rows: One slot and Worker upgrade available
Worker tech, war_effort, plus tier currency-system prerequisites

sections.title: Additional slot-two requirements
paragraphs: The helper starts with war_effort. Based on DEFAULT tier currency, it then adds requisition_office for Requisition, war_effort for Medals, quest_board for Rings, or dungeon for Ducats. Duplicated war_effort entries are possible. Later per-node currency overrides do not recalculate that list.

sections.title: Quality variants
paragraphs: Mine, resource suppliers, Forest, Farm, Barracks recruiting, and Training Grounds use specialized Artisan types. Normal crafting uses Artisan. Productivity wording depends on whether the machine processes equipment and enhancements. Individual machine branches can substitute specialized upgrades and slot rules. The tier articles preserve helper calls and post-creation overrides.

articles.title: Technology cost formula
articles.summary: Deterministic prices, type multipliers, currency conversion, rounding, and prestige.

sections.title: Raw price
paragraphs: At technology cost tier t, P = 400 × typeMultiplier × CostMultiplier × 2^(t−1) × R. R is a deterministic pseudorandom float in [0.92,1.10), seeded from the identifier. Prices do not reroll whenever a menu opens. A zero multiplier creates a free empty collection. Gold numbers in this formula are stored smallest-coin units: 100 units = 1 silver and 10,000 = 1 displayed gold coin.

sections.title: Each currency is a separate charge
paragraphs: Gold = RoundGold(truncate(P × GoldMultiplier × (1 if tier≤1 else 2))). Each non-gold charge is ceil(P/referenceGoldValue); Faith and Ingenuity are then halved with integer division. Gold plus Ducats means both charges, not a split total.
Normal RoundGold leaves values below 10,000 unchanged, rounds 10,000–999,999 to hundreds, and rounds 1,000,000 or more to ten-thousands. The helper supports another maxCount mode for other callers.

sections.title: Prestige and caching
paragraphs: TechCostReduce multiplies the generated collection by 1−perkValue and rounds each result with Math.Round. TechNode caches costs; GameManager resets every cached cost at scene start. Explicit currency/multiplier overrides take priority. Non-technology buildings share CreateCost but use a different tier-scaling branch.

articles.title: Currencies and currency exchange
articles.summary: All nine currencies and exact exchange rates and taxes.

headers: Reference value in raw Gold units

sections.title: Reference values
paragraphs: Values convert generated gold-equivalent costs into secondary currency amounts and provide exchange base rates. Balances and earned totals are separate. Spending a collection first checks affordability of every included currency.

sections.title: Exchange
paragraphs: currency_exchange follows Inventor; currency_exchange_tax follows it. Base tax is 1.0 (100%). Tax research halves it to 0.5. Prestige then multiplies tax by 1−CurrencyTaxReduce value.

Buying A units at reference value V costs truncate(A×V×(1+tax)) raw Gold units. Selling yields truncate(A×V/(1+tax)). At base tax, a Requisition costs 2,000 raw units (20 silver) and sells for 500 (5 silver); with only tax research it costs 1,500 (15 silver) and sells for 666 (6 silver, 66 copper).

sections.title: Income statistics
paragraphs: Exchange outputs use isIncome=false and do not count as earned Gold. Buy slider maximum uses affordable Gold; sell maximum uses currency balance.

paragraphs: Retained technologies go through AddTech again, so OnUnlock effects run for the new player. A Utility that adds workflows or machine capabilities can have those effects again. The retention filter checks the exact NodeType, not whether the name sounds like automation.

sections.title: Active nightmare display
paragraphs: NightmareCountActive is an ascension snapshot used to display newly gained nightmares as a +difference. Endgame multipliers use total NightmareCount, so newly earned nightmares can affect later runs before ascending.

articles.title: Prestige perks and refunds
articles.summary: All nine perks and their exact rank formulas.

sections.title: Ranks and refunds
paragraphs: A zero-point perk has zero effect. Rank n costs n nightmares: first rank 1, second 2, third 3. Total rank-n investment is n(n+1)/2. Unspent nightmares equal total NightmareCount minus all invested rank costs. Left click buys a rank when affordable; right click refunds a rank; Reset sets every perk to zero.

sections.title: Application
paragraphs: Research discount multiplies generated research currency collections. Resource discount is read by player resource upgrades, Forest crew upgrades, and Farm upgrades. Human quality is added during human resource generation; equipment and dark-essence quality are added in the relevant crafting-result creation. Human health is included in HumanItemData health calculation; sell value is read by Shop and LuxuryShop. Manual productivity is read by RecipeElement. Manual crafting adds the perk value to current Productivity before accumulating productivity progress; equipment manually receives a further ×0.5 factor.
The purchase handler has no explicit per-perk rank cap. The formulas above are literal source behavior; extrapolated extreme ranks are not balanced-design recommendations.

articles.title: Nightmares and the endgame loop
articles.summary: Distilled nightmares, fragments, distiller charging, and enemy scaling.

sections.title: Earning nightmares
paragraphs: The endgame dungeon final boss lists FragmentedNightmareReward and DistilledNightmareReward. Distilled reward is ready when NightmareActive and NightmareProgress>0.99, or unconditionally when total nightmares are zero. Receiving it increases the total, updates the Steam stat, subtracts 1 charge if charge≥1, partially resets North war, and opens the victory popup for the first nightmare.

Fragmented reward creates fragmented_nightmare with chance 1 and amount 2. It is enabled while nightmare mode is active, or while the total is zero. The quest overloads for both rewards are empty; their dungeon overloads perform the reward.

sections.title: The distiller
paragraphs: nightmare_distiller follows dungeon_endgame and additionally checks that the last endgame CompletedCount entry is positive. The machine class is NightmareCollector, displayed as nightmare_distiller. Its one-item input consumes nightmare_collector items.

Below full charge, each consumed item adds 1/floor(sqrt(totalNightmares)). Values between 0.985 and 1 are snapped to 1. At 1–3 nightmares each item fills a charge, at 4–8 it fills half, and at 9–15 it fills one-third. The machine Update itself does not check NightmareActive; reward eligibility and enemy multipliers do.

sections.title: Toggle and repeat access
paragraphs: The distiller UI toggles NightmareActive. Difficulty readers require IsEndgame and NightmareActive. A distilled reward changes North war from stage index 4 back to 3; when at index 3, progress is set to 10. This partial reset requires the final war section to be secured again, independently of ascension.
